title: Atal Pension Yojana 2026: Rs. 5,000/month, Extended till 2031
ministry: Ministry of Finance (PFRDA)
eligibility: 18 to 40 years
Savings bank account required
Aadhaar required
Not an income tax payer
benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000-₹5,000 from age 60
Spouse pension on subscriber death
Lump sum corpus to nominee after both subscriber and spouse pass away
documents: Aadhaar card
Savings bank account details
Mobile number linked to bank account
Nominee details
description: Atal Pension Yojana 2026 gives guaranteed monthly pension of Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 after 60. Cabinet extended scheme till FY 2030-31. 9.10 crore enrolled.
content:
## What Atal Pension Yojana is

Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a government-backed pension scheme for workers in the unorganised sector. It guarantees a fixed monthly pension between Rs. 1,000 and Rs. 5,000 after the subscriber turns 60, in exchange for monthly contributions between age 18 and 40. The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) administers the scheme, and any bank or post office savings account can be used to enrol.

As of 18 May 2026, APY has 9.10 crore gross enrolments and total assets under management above Rs. 54,000 crore, per PFRDA. FY26 added 1.35 crore new subscribers, the highest single-year addition since APY launched in 2015.

APY replaced the earlier Swavalamban Yojana in 2015 and covers more low and middle-income Indians than any other voluntary retirement product regulated by PFRDA. The pension amount is not a projection or a market return. It's a legally-guaranteed monthly payout for life, funded by the subscriber's contribution stream and a central government backstop.

---

## Cabinet extended APY till FY 2030-31

On 21 January 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the continuation of Atal Pension Yojana till FY 2030-31 and cleared gap-funding support for the scheme's promotional and developmental activities, per PIB PRID 2216727. The extension answers what happens to APY after the original 2025-26 fund-support window.

For existing subscribers, the extension changes nothing about your contribution amount or pension terms. Your promised pension continues under the same rules you enrolled under. The extension matters for new enrolments in 2026 and beyond, since APY now has a clear five-year runway with committed government support for administrative costs and PFRDA's promotional push in rural areas.

Alongside the extension, PFRDA is reviewing a proposal to raise the maximum pension slab from Rs. 5,000 to a higher figure. As of mid-2026, no notification has been issued, but Outlook Money and other financial press have reported the reform is under active PFRDA consideration. Existing subscribers can migrate to the higher slab if it goes through, though contribution amounts would need to be recalculated for the extra corpus.

---

## Who can join APY

Four rules decide APY eligibility.

You must be between 18 and 40 years old on the date of enrolment. Below 18 you can't enrol; at 41 or older the scheme is closed to you. Anyone in the 18 to 40 window with a valid savings bank or post office account can apply.

You need an Aadhaar-linked mobile number. Aadhaar is used for e-KYC at enrolment, and monthly SMS confirmations of the auto-debit go to the linked mobile.

You can't be an income taxpayer. Since 1 October 2022, individuals who have filed an income tax return in the preceding financial year are barred from new APY enrolment. Existing pre-2022 subscribers who now file ITR are grandfathered in, but no new enrolments open for taxpayers.

You must consent to an auto-debit mandate on your bank or post office account. APY contributions are pulled automatically each month, with no manual payment option.

The typical APY subscriber is a domestic worker, farmer, driver, small shopkeeper, factory worker, self-employed tradesperson, or private-sector low-wage employee. Government employees under NPS and formal-sector workers under EPFO are usually better served by their existing scheme rather than APY.

---

## Contribution chart: what you pay each month

Your monthly contribution depends on two variables: the pension slab you choose (Rs. 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000, or 5,000 per month after 60), and your age at enrolment. The lower the entry age, the lower your monthly contribution for the same pension.

The canonical PFRDA contribution chart is below (all figures in rupees per month):

| Entry age | Rs. 1,000 pension | Rs. 2,000 pension | Rs. 3,000 pension | Rs. 4,000 pension | Rs. 5,000 pension |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18 | 42 | 84 | 126 | 168 | 210 |
| 20 | 50 | 100 | 150 | 198 | 248 |
| 25 | 76 | 151 | 226 | 301 | 376 |
| 30 | 116 | 231 | 347 | 462 | 577 |
| 35 | 181 | 362 | 543 | 722 | 902 |
| 40 | 291 | 582 | 873 | 1,164 | 1,454 |

Source: NSDL APY Subscribers Contribution Chart (npscra.nsdl.co.in).

The contribution stays fixed for the entire deferment period. You can't pause and resume, and you can't vary the amount month to month.

You can switch pension slabs once a year on 1 April. Upgrading from Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 3,000 for a 30-year-old, for example, would raise the monthly contribution from Rs. 231 to Rs. 347. Downgrading is also allowed once a year on the same date.

---

## Worked example: pension math at three entry ages

Concrete numbers make APY easier to compare against other retirement products. Three scenarios computed on the PFRDA base chart show the effect of entry age.

An 18-year-old on the Rs. 1,000 pension slab pays Rs. 42 per month for 42 years to age 60. Total contribution comes to Rs. 21,168. Guaranteed pension is Rs. 1,000 per month for life after 60. On subscriber death, the spouse gets the same Rs. 1,000; on spouse death, the nominee gets the returnable corpus of approximately Rs. 1.7 lakh (per PFRDA formula).

A 25-year-old on the Rs. 3,000 pension slab pays Rs. 226 per month for 35 years. Total contribution comes to Rs. 94,920. Guaranteed pension is Rs. 3,000 per month for life. Returnable corpus to nominee is approximately Rs. 5.1 lakh.

A 40-year-old on the Rs. 5,000 pension slab pays Rs. 1,454 per month for 20 years. Total contribution comes to Rs. 3.49 lakh. Guaranteed pension is Rs. 5,000 per month for life. Returnable corpus to nominee is approximately Rs. 8.5 lakh.

The younger the entry age, the higher the effective return on contribution. The 18-year-old puts in Rs. 21,168 across a working life and draws pension for 20+ years plus leaves Rs. 1.7 lakh corpus. The 40-year-old puts in Rs. 3.49 lakh across 20 years for the same monthly pension pattern.

The returnable corpus is a distinct feature of APY versus most other Indian pension products. On spouse death after the subscriber's death, the corpus goes to the nominee as a lump sum. Neither the subscriber nor spouse can withdraw the corpus while alive. This design keeps the guaranteed monthly pension solvent for every participant in the pool.

---

## What happens if you miss auto-debit

APY assumes the auto-debit succeeds every month. If your bank account has insufficient balance on the debit date, penalty and freeze rules kick in.

The penalty starts at Re 1 per Rs. 100 missed for pension slabs Rs. 1,000 and Rs. 2,000, rises to Rs. 2 per Rs. 100 for the Rs. 3,000 slab, Rs. 5 per Rs. 100 for the Rs. 4,000 slab, and Rs. 10 per Rs. 100 for the Rs. 5,000 slab.

If contributions are missed for 6 continuous months, the account is frozen. You can still make a lump-sum payment for the missed months plus penalty to unfreeze it.

After 12 months of continuous missed contributions, the account is deactivated. Reactivation requires PFRDA nodal-bank approval and full penalty payment.

After 24 continuous months of default, the account is closed. The subscriber's contributions plus interest are returned to the bank account, and pension entitlement is lost.

The simplest way to avoid all of the above is to keep at least three months' worth of contributions in the linked bank account as buffer, especially around your annual bonus or salary hike when the account balance can dip.

---

## How to enrol in APY

Two paths lead to APY enrolment: through your bank or post office branch, or through the online net-banking portal of banks that support digital APY registration.

The branch path starts at any nationalised, private, or cooperative bank where you have a savings account. Ask for the APY subscriber registration form (SRF). Fill in your Aadhaar number, mobile number, chosen pension slab, and auto-debit consent. The branch employee submits the form to the bank's APY nodal desk and issues an acknowledgement number. Your APY account is activated within 3 to 5 working days, and the first monthly contribution is debited automatically.

The online path works inside the net-banking apps of SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, PNB, Bank of Baroda, and Union Bank. Log in, look for PMSBY / PMJJBY / APY in the insurance-scheme menu, enter Aadhaar and OTP, choose pension slab, and confirm the auto-debit consent. The account is active from the next debit cycle.

The documents needed are an Aadhaar card, an Aadhaar-linked mobile number, a savings bank or post office account, and a self-declaration of non-taxpayer status. No income proof, no PAN card, no separate address proof.

Once the account is active, the bank issues a Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) and mails a physical statement of accounts annually. You can also check the account online at npscra.nsdl.co.in using PRAN and date of birth.

---

## Withdrawal and exit rules

APY is designed as a long-hold pension product. Exit rules reflect that design.

At regular exit at 60, the subscriber starts receiving the guaranteed monthly pension for life from the month after they turn 60. Pension is credited via NEFT to the linked bank account and continues till the subscriber's death.

On subscriber death, the spouse becomes the default nominee and receives the same monthly pension for life. On spouse death, the returnable corpus (per PFRDA formula) goes to the nominated beneficiary as a lump sum.

Voluntary exit before 60 is only allowed in exceptional cases: terminal illness of the subscriber or death of the subscriber before 60. In terminal illness cases, the accumulated contributions and any interest are returned to the subscriber, and pension entitlement is closed. This is the only pre-60 exit path for a living subscriber.

If the subscriber dies before 60, the spouse can either continue the account by paying remaining contributions until the subscriber would have turned 60 and then draw pension for life, or withdraw the accumulated corpus immediately.

APY doesn't allow partial withdrawals, loans against corpus, or premature exits for personal financial emergencies. The rules exist to keep the guaranteed pension solvent for every subscriber in the pool.

---

## Tax benefit under Section 80CCD

Contributions to Atal Pension Yojana qualify for tax deduction under Section 80CCD of the Income Tax Act. Two provisions apply.

Under Section 80CCD(1), APY contributions count within the overall Rs. 1.5 lakh deduction under Section 80C. This isn't an additional benefit. APY simply becomes eligible for the same pool that also holds LIC premium, EPF, PPF, and ELSS.

Under Section 80CCD(1B), an additional Rs. 50,000 deduction is available for APY and NPS contributions above the Rs. 1.5 lakh 80C limit. This is a separate ceiling and stacks on top of 80C.

The taxpayer paradox is that since 1 October 2022, income taxpayers cannot enrol in new APY accounts. Existing pre-2022 subscribers who now file ITR can still claim the deduction on their ongoing contributions. New enrolments are restricted to non-taxpayers, who by definition earn below the Rs. 2.5 lakh basic-exemption threshold and rarely have significant tax to save.

For a Rs. 5,000 pension slab at entry age 25, the annual contribution is Rs. 376 x 12 = Rs. 4,512. For a 40-year entry with the same slab, annual contribution is Rs. 1,454 x 12 = Rs. 17,448. Both fit inside 80CCD(1) if the subscriber ever crosses the tax threshold in later years.

---

## APY vs NPS Vatsalya vs PMVVY: how they compare

APY sits alongside two other government-backed retirement products. The three are worth comparing side by side.

| Feature | APY | NPS Vatsalya | PMVVY (closed to new enrolments Mar 2023) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target user | Unorganised sector adult 18 to 40 | Minor children 0 to 18 | Senior citizen 60+ |
| Pension guarantee | Yes, Rs. 1,000 to 5,000 fixed slab | No, market-linked corpus | Yes, 7.4% fixed for 10 years |
| Contribution period | Till age 60 | Till child turns 18 (then convert to NPS) | Lump-sum purchase |
| Return-of-corpus | Yes, to nominee after spouse | Yes, at 60 to subscriber | Yes, at 10 years to nominee |
| Tax benefit | 80CCD | 80CCD | 80C |
| Regulator | PFRDA | PFRDA | LIC |
| Withdrawal before term | Only on terminal illness or death | Restricted till 18 | 3 years partial |

APY fits if you are 18 to 40, not a taxpayer, want guaranteed monthly pension after 60, can commit to an unbroken auto-debit for 20 to 40 years, and are comfortable with pension capped at Rs. 5,000/month.

NPS Vatsalya fits if you are a parent starting retirement savings for a young child, willing to accept market-linked returns, and want to lock the money till 18.

PMVVY fits if you were already 60+ before 31 March 2023, already have an existing PMVVY policy, and want to complete the 10-year fixed-return term. New enrolments have been closed since 31 March 2023.

---

## Common rejection reasons for APY enrolment

Applications get rejected at the bank nodal desk stage for a small set of common issues. Fixing these upfront saves a re-submission cycle.

The most common rejection is an Aadhaar and mobile mismatch. The Aadhaar on the SRF must match the mobile number the OTP was sent to. Update your mobile at the Aadhaar seva kendra if there is a mismatch.

The taxpayer status flag catches anyone who filed an income tax return in the preceding financial year. This is verified through PAN linkage with the Aadhaar backend. Non-filers who receive Form 16 from an employer but did not file ITR are still eligible.

Age outside the 18 to 40 window is checked on the date of enrolment using the Aadhaar date of birth. 40 years plus 1 day is rejected. Below 18 the SRF cannot even be submitted.

Joint account attempts are rejected because APY is a single-holder product. Joint bank accounts cannot be used for auto-debit. Open a single-holder account first and then apply.

Duplicate PRAN triggers rejection because one person can hold only one APY account. If the Aadhaar is already linked to an APY PRAN, the new SRF is rejected. If you want to move to a different bank, use the inter-bank shift form rather than opening a fresh account.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**Am I eligible for Atal Pension Yojana in 2026?** You qualify if you are 18 to 40 years old, an Indian citizen with a savings bank or post office account, and not an income taxpayer. Aadhaar and a linked mobile number are also mandatory.

**What is the current maximum APY pension?** Rs. 5,000 per month for life after age 60. PFRDA is reviewing a higher slab in 2026, but no notification has been issued yet.

**How is APY different from NPS?** APY is a small-corpus, guaranteed-pension scheme aimed at the unorganised sector. NPS is a market-linked accumulation scheme with no guaranteed pension amount and is used by government employees and higher-income private-sector workers. Both are regulated by PFRDA.

**Can I hold both APY and NPS accounts?** Yes. There is no conflict, and both accounts can be held simultaneously. Each has its own PRAN.

**What happens if I stop APY contributions?** Penalty accrues per missed month at Re 1 to Rs. 10 per Rs. 100 depending on your slab. After 6 months of continuous default the account is frozen, after 12 months it is deactivated, and after 24 months it is closed with only contributions plus interest returned.

**Is Atal Pension Yojana taxable?** Contributions qualify for deduction under Section 80CCD. The pension received after 60 is taxable as income under normal income-tax rules.

**Can I withdraw APY money before 60?** Only in specific cases: terminal illness of the subscriber (accumulated contributions returned), or death of the subscriber before 60 (spouse can continue or withdraw the corpus). Voluntary withdrawal for other reasons is not allowed.

**Which bank should I open APY at?** Any bank or post office where you already have a savings account. The bank does not affect pension amount or subscription terms since PFRDA runs the pool centrally.

**Is APY safe if the scheme faces a funding gap?** APY contributions are pooled and invested by PFRDA in a regulated pension fund. The government's guaranteed pension is a legal commitment. In the case of any shortfall between actual corpus and promised pension, the central government funds the difference from budget resources.

**How do I check my APY account balance and PRAN statement?** Log in to npscra.nsdl.co.in with PRAN and date of birth. The e-statement shows total contributions, latest contribution, and projected pension based on current contribution pattern. The physical annual statement is also mailed to the linked address.

---

Step 3: Use the Awaas+ mobile app to register a grievance if your name was excluded despite eligibility. Step 4: After selection, complete Aadhaar-linked bank account registration. description: PMAY-G 2026 gives rural families Rs. 1.20 to 1.30 lakh to build a pucca house. 3.90 crore sanctioned, 2.99 crore complete. Target 4.95 crore homes by 2029.
content:
## What PMAY-G is

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Gramin (PMAY-G) is the central government's rural housing mission. It provides direct financial assistance to households that don't own a pucca house, so they can build a permanent home with basic amenities like a toilet, LPG connection, drinking water, and electricity. The Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) runs the scheme through state rural development departments and gram panchayats.

As of 26 March 2026, PMAY-G has sanctioned 3.90 crore houses and completed 2.99 crore of them, per the MoRD dashboard at dashboard.dord.gov.in. The scheme has generated 568 crore person-days of rural employment between 2016 and 2025, MoRD reports.

PMAY-G replaced the earlier Indira Awas Yojana (IAY) in April 2016. The unit assistance was raised, the beneficiary list was moved to the SECC 2011 database, and construction quality standards were tightened with a mandatory pucca structure of 25 square metres minimum. Payment shifted to direct benefit transfer (DBT) in three instalments linked to construction milestones verified through geo-tagged photographs.

---

## PMAY-G 2.0: target upgraded to 4.95 crore houses by 2029

The Union Cabinet approved PMAY-G 2.0 in August 2024, extending the scheme's runway to March 2029 and raising the cumulative target from 2.95 crore houses to 4.95 crore houses. This adds 2 crore fresh sanctions on top of the balance from the first phase, per PIB releases.

Budget 2026-27 allocates Rs. 54,916.70 crore to PMAY-G, up 266.1% from the Rs. 15,000 crore allocation in 2016-17 when the scheme first launched. This is the largest annual outlay in the scheme's history and funds the accelerated construction schedule PMAY-G 2.0 requires.

The upgrade responds to two data points. First, the AwaasPlus 2024 self-survey identified more genuinely eligible households than the original SECC 2011 base captured. Second, states with near-saturation of the SECC 2011 list, such as Uttar Pradesh at 36.40 lakh of 36.85 lakh target, asked for a fresh allocation cycle. The 4.95 crore ceiling gives every state a second window to add left-out households discovered in the new survey.

For beneficiaries already sanctioned under the first phase, PMAY-G 2.0 doesn't change the unit assistance amount or the 3-instalment DBT structure. It only adds new applicants to the pipeline.

---

## Who qualifies for PMAY-G

Eligibility runs off two databases. Households on the SECC 2011 Automatic Inclusion or deprivation-parameter list were the original PMAY-G intake source. The AwaasPlus 2024 self-survey added new households not captured by SECC 2011.

To qualify, the household must be either houseless, or living in a kutcha or dilapidated house with zero or one room, no pucca wall, or no pucca roof. Automatic inclusion covers households with no adult earning member of working age, no literate adult above 25, or a member from a manual scavenger, PVTG, or bonded labour category.

Automatic exclusion applies if the household has a motorised two, three, or four-wheeler; a mechanised three or four-wheeler agricultural implement; a Kisan Credit Card with limit above Rs. 50,000; a member as a government employee or drawing over Rs. 10,000 per month; a member paying income tax or professional tax; owning a refrigerator, landline phone, or 2.5 acres of irrigated land, or 5 acres of unirrigated land; or a pucca house of three rooms or more with pucca walls and pucca roof.

The beneficiary must be an Indian citizen. Priority within the eligible pool goes to SC, ST, minorities, widows, next of kin of defence personnel killed in action, disabled persons, and families in LWE-affected districts as per the standing allocation policy.

Ownership of the sanctioned house is registered in the woman member's name, or jointly with her husband, unless the household has no adult female member.

---

## AwaasPlus 2024 self-survey mobile app

The AwaasPlus 2024 mobile app is the current intake channel for new PMAY-G applicants. It replaces the earlier paper-form and gram sabha route for fresh registrations, and it works alongside SECC 2011 records for beneficiaries already on the list.

The app uses Aadhaar face authentication as the primary identity check. A household head opens the app on any smartphone, enters the Aadhaar number, and completes a live face scan matched against the Aadhaar biometric backend. Once the face match passes, the household details, member list, income declaration, and existing housing status can be entered.

Field surveyors visit each self-surveyed household to verify the entered details, geo-tag the current dwelling, and upload photographs. The gram sabha then reviews the verified list at a public meeting and forwards approvals to the block office.

Households without smartphones can still register through the panchayat secretary or the block Awas Sahayak. The Sahayak carries an Android tablet with the app pre-installed and completes the survey on behalf of the household.

The AwaasPlus 2024 data feeds directly into the AwaasSoft MIS at awaassoft.nic.in, which is the same MIS that tracks sanctioned houses, DBT release, and construction progress across all states.

---

## What you get: unit assistance breakdown

PMAY-G unit assistance depends on the geography of the beneficiary's village.

For plain areas, the central and state governments together pay Rs. 1.20 lakh per house, split 60:40 for most states and 90:10 for the eight north-eastern states, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh. Union Territories get 100% central funding.

For hilly, north-eastern, and Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) affected districts, the unit assistance rises to Rs. 1.30 lakh per house. This covers 24 of the 28 states and all UTs, per MoRD.

Beyond the base unit assistance, PMAY-G beneficiaries receive Rs. 12,000 under Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin (SBM-G) for a household toilet, converged from the ministry's parallel sanitation programme. They're also entitled to about 90 to 95 days of unskilled MGNREGA wages toward house construction, and a free LPG connection under Ujjwala for the same household.

Grid electricity, tap water under Jal Jeevan Mission, and access to a pension scheme like PMSYM or NSAP are converged alongside PMAY-G at the same beneficiary level, so the family ends up with a full basic-amenities package rather than only walls and a roof.

---

## Worked example: full Rs. 1.90 lakh package math

For a plain-area beneficiary in a district like Muzaffarpur, Bihar, the full effective package works out as follows.

Unit assistance from PMAY-G comes to Rs. 1,20,000, released in three DBT instalments to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account.

SBM-G toilet component adds Rs. 12,000, disbursed once the toilet is constructed and geo-tagged.

MGNREGA wages for house construction come to about Rs. 90 days x Rs. 245 average state wage rate = Rs. 22,050. The exact figure varies by state notified wage. Bihar notified 2025-26 MGNREGA wage is Rs. 245 per day, per the Ministry of Rural Development notification.

Free LPG connection under Ujjwala carries a cash-equivalent of about Rs. 3,200 including refill support in the first year.

Grid electricity connection under Saubhagya (now completed nationally) and Jal Jeevan Mission tap connection carry an implicit household benefit of Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 20,000, depending on distance to the mains.

Adding the direct cash and toilet component and MGNREGA wages gives Rs. 1,20,000 + Rs. 12,000 + Rs. 22,050 = Rs. 1,54,050. Adding LPG and utility convergence takes the effective package to about Rs. 1,90,000 per beneficiary in plain areas.

In hilly, NE, and LWE areas the base rises to Rs. 1,30,000, taking the effective package to about Rs. 2,00,000.

The 25 square metres minimum built area is a scheme rule. Beneficiaries who build larger houses meet the extra cost from their own savings or MGNREGA labour input, since the unit assistance is capped.

---

## Fund-flow timeline: instalment release schedule

PMAY-G pays the unit assistance in three DBT instalments, each tied to a construction milestone verified through the AwaasSoft MIS.

The first instalment is 25% of unit assistance, or Rs. 30,000 in plain areas and Rs. 32,500 in hilly, NE, LWE areas. It's released within seven days of sanction and Aadhaar-linked bank verification, once the beneficiary uploads the "start" geo-tagged photograph showing the plot.

The second instalment is 60% of unit assistance, or Rs. 72,000 in plain areas and Rs. 78,000 in hilly, NE, LWE areas. It's released after the plinth or lintel level is reached, with a geo-tagged photograph showing the milestone. Typical trigger is 60 to 90 days from the first instalment.

The third and final instalment is 15% of unit assistance, or Rs. 18,000 in plain areas and Rs. 19,500 in hilly, NE, LWE areas. It's released after roof completion, plaster, floor, and toilet are verified with a completion geo-tagged photograph. Typical trigger is 90 to 180 days from the second instalment, depending on availability of materials and labour.

If construction stops between instalments, the state's Awas Sahayak issues a written notice to the beneficiary. Continued non-response can lead to sanction cancellation and recovery of released funds, though state officers usually try to route MGNREGA labour or masonry training first.

---

## Common rejection reasons

Applications and sanctions are rejected at the AwaasSoft verification stage for a small number of recurring causes. Fixing the underlying issue upfront saves a rejection cycle.

Pucca house already detected is the most frequent rejection. The field surveyor's geo-tagged photograph shows a pucca structure with pucca walls and pucca roof of three rooms or more, which triggers automatic exclusion under the SECC 2011 parameters.

Motorised four-wheeler ownership is checked through the vehicle registration database. If any household member owns a car, jeep, or SUV, the household is excluded regardless of income declaration.

Kisan Credit Card with limit above Rs. 50,000 is picked up from the KCC database. Households with a higher-limit KCC are excluded, even if the actual disbursement is lower.

Government employee in the household leads to exclusion. This includes central, state, and PSU employees, but not part-time contractual workers below Rs. 10,000 per month.

Name and Aadhaar mismatch is the most fixable rejection. If the beneficiary name on the AwaasPlus survey differs from the Aadhaar record even by a spelling variation, the sanction is held up. Correction at the Aadhaar seva kendra, followed by resubmission of the AwaasPlus record, usually clears the block within two weeks.

---

## PMAY-G vs PMAY-U: how they compare

PMAY-G targets rural households, while Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Urban (PMAY-U) targets urban families. The two schemes have distinct rules despite the shared brand.

| Feature | PMAY-G | PMAY-U |
|---|---|---|
| Target beneficiary | Rural households without pucca house | Urban households EWS, LIG, MIG |
| Ministry | Rural Development (MoRD) | Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) |
| Unit assistance | Rs. 1.20 to 1.30 lakh, DBT | Rs. 1 to 2.67 lakh depending on vertical |
| Verticals | Single (new construction) | Four (ISSR, CLSS, AHP, BLC) |
| Eligibility base | SECC 2011 plus AwaasPlus 2024 | Self-declaration plus income proof |
| Ownership | Woman member or joint | Woman member or joint |
| Phase 2 | PMAY-G 2.0 till March 2029 | PMAY-U 2.0 till 2028-29 |
| Sanction as of Mar 2026 | 3.90 crore | 1.19 crore |

PMAY-G runs a single vertical, which is new construction. PMAY-U runs four verticals: in-situ slum redevelopment (ISSR), credit-linked subsidy scheme (CLSS), affordable housing in partnership (AHP), and beneficiary-led construction (BLC).

A household near a rural-urban boundary should apply under the scheme that matches the panchayat or municipal jurisdiction of the plot address. Applying under the wrong scheme leads to rejection at the sanction stage.

---

## State-wise completion league table

Completion progress varies sharply across states, driven by state administrative capacity, panchayat responsiveness, and construction-material logistics. The MoRD dashboard tracks live completion by state.

| State | Sanctioned target (lakh) | Completed (lakh) | Completion % |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uttar Pradesh | 36.85 | 36.40 | 98.8% |
| Madhya Pradesh | 57.74 | 40.55 | 70.2% |
| Bihar | 50.12 | 39.14 | 78.1% |
| West Bengal | 45.69 | 34.20 | 74.8% |
| Arunachal Pradesh | 0.36 | 0.36 | 100.0% |

Arunachal Pradesh reported 100% completion of its 35,591 house target in June 2026, per the Chief Minister's statement. It's the first state to hit full saturation of the SECC 2011 list ahead of PMAY-G 2.0's fresh allocation cycle.

Uttar Pradesh is near saturation of its Phase 1 target, and 45,000 houses remain in the pipeline. Madhya Pradesh has the largest absolute target at 57.74 lakh and the largest absolute completion at 40.55 lakh. Bihar and West Bengal are in the 70 to 80% band and are expected to close their Phase 1 lists within 2026-27.

Northern states in the hilly and NE band such as Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim run smaller absolute programs but at higher unit-assistance rates. Completion percentages in these states track alongside the plain-area averages.

---

## How to check your PMAY-G application status

Beneficiaries can check status through three channels.

The AwaasSoft portal at awaassoft.nic.in has a beneficiary search page. Enter the registration number or Aadhaar number to see the sanction status, instalment dates, and any pending verification.

The PMAY-G dashboard at dashboard.dord.gov.in/dashboardnew/pmayg.aspx shows aggregate progress by state, district, and block. Individual beneficiary data isn't shown on the public dashboard, but the district and block officer can pull the record with the beneficiary's Aadhaar number.

The AwaasPlus mobile app carries a status tab for households registered under the 2024 self-survey. Log in with Aadhaar face authentication to see the current status of the household application.

For DBT tracking, the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) at pfms.nic.in shows credit into the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account. Reference number and date can be shared with the branch if the credit doesn't reflect in the passbook.

---

## How to apply

Three paths lead to a PMAY-G application, depending on the beneficiary's current status.

New applicants without an SECC 2011 record should install the AwaasPlus 2024 mobile app on a smartphone, complete the Aadhaar face authentication, and enter household details. Field surveyor verification follows within four to six weeks in most districts.

Households on the SECC 2011 permanent waitlist for their block should visit the panchayat secretary or the Awas Sahayak. The Sahayak checks the SECC 2011 record, matches it against the AwaasSoft MIS, and initiates a sanction request through the block office.

Applicants seeking a corrections update, such as bank account change, spouse addition, or death of the original beneficiary, should visit the panchayat secretary with an Aadhaar photocopy, a fresh bank account passbook copy, and the earlier PMAY-G sanction letter.

The AwaasSoft MIS is the backend for all three paths. Beneficiaries who complete the survey but don't see status updates for over 60 days should escalate to the district Awas Sahayak or the district Zilla Parishad CEO's office.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**Am I eligible for PMAY-G in 2026?** You qualify if your household doesn't own a pucca house, is on the SECC 2011 deprivation or automatic inclusion list, or is registered on the AwaasPlus 2024 self-survey, and doesn't hit any of the automatic exclusion parameters like four-wheeler ownership or a KCC limit above Rs. 50,000.

**How much money do I get under PMAY-G?** Rs. 1.20 lakh per house in plain areas and Rs. 1.30 lakh in hilly, NE, and LWE areas, paid in three DBT instalments tied to construction milestones. An additional Rs. 12,000 for a toilet under SBM-G and about 90 to 95 days of MGNREGA wages take the effective package to about Rs. 1.90 lakh.

**What is PMAY-G 2.0?** It's the extended phase approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024, which raises the cumulative PMAY-G target from 2.95 crore houses to 4.95 crore houses by March 2029 and allocates Rs. 54,916.70 crore in Budget 2026-27.

**How do I apply through the AwaasPlus 2024 mobile app?** Install the AwaasPlus 2024 app, enter your Aadhaar number, complete the live face scan, and enter household and housing details. Field surveyor verification follows within four to six weeks in most districts.

**Can I get PMAY-G if I already have a small pucca house?** No, if the pucca structure has three rooms or more and pucca walls plus pucca roof. Households with a smaller kutcha or dilapidated dwelling are eligible.

**What's the DBT instalment schedule?** 25% on sanction and start of construction, 60% at plinth or lintel level, and 15% on roof and completion. Each release requires a geo-tagged photograph uploaded through the AwaasSoft MIS.

**Why was my PMAY-G application rejected?** The five common reasons are pucca house detected on the ground survey, motorised four-wheeler in the household, KCC limit above Rs. 50,000, a government employee in the household, or a name-Aadhaar mismatch. The mismatch case can be fixed at an Aadhaar seva kendra.

**How is PMAY-G different from PMAY-U?** PMAY-G is for rural households and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development. PMAY-U is for urban households and is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. PMAY-G runs a single new-construction vertical. PMAY-U runs four verticals covering slum redevelopment, credit-linked subsidy, affordable partnership housing, and beneficiary-led construction.

**How do I check my PMAY-G status online?** Use the beneficiary search on awaassoft.nic.in with the registration number or Aadhaar number, or check DBT credit history at pfms.nic.in. The PMAY-G public dashboard at dashboard.dord.gov.in shows aggregate progress but not individual records.

**Is the PMAY-G house registered in the woman's name?** Yes, sanction ownership is registered in the woman member's name, or jointly with her husband, unless the household has no adult female member.

---

## Official links and helplines

| Purpose | Link or number |
|---|---|
| Official PMAY-G portal | pmayg.nic.in |
| AwaasSoft beneficiary MIS | awaassoft.nic.in |
| PMAY-G live dashboard | dashboard.dord.gov.in/dashboardnew/pmayg.aspx |
| AwaasPlus 2024 mobile app | Google Play Store, search "AwaasPlus 2024" |

description: PM Rozgar Mela has issued about 12 lakh appointment letters, but it has no form to fill. Find out what it actually is and the real routes into those jobs.
content:
## PM Rozgar Mela: there is no application form

Rozgar Mela is a recruitment drive under which the Prime Minister distributes appointment letters to people newly appointed to central government posts. It was launched on 22 October 2022 with a target of recruiting 10 lakh personnel in mission mode, and at that first event appointment letters went to about 75,000 appointees.

Now the part that matters most, because a great deal of what is published about this is wrong.

You cannot apply to Rozgar Mela. There is no Rozgar Mela registration, no online form, no eligibility criteria and no last date. Search results promising a "PM Rojgar Mela online form" or "Rozgar Mela registration 2026" are describing something that does not exist.

Rozgar Mela is the ceremony at which appointment letters are handed over. Every person receiving a letter there was already selected through a normal recruitment process: an SSC examination, a UPSC examination, a Railway Recruitment Board CEN, an IBPS examination, or a departmental recruitment. The mela is the last step of that journey, not an entry point to it.

If your goal is one of those jobs, the route is the recruitment examination, and this page sets out which ones actually feed into it.

## What has happened so far

| Milestone | Detail |
|---|---|
| Launched | 22 October 2022, by the Prime Minister via video conferencing |
| Stated target | 10 lakh personnel, recruited in mission mode |
| First edition | About 75,000 appointment letters |
| 18th edition | 24 January 2026, more than 61,000 letters |
| 19th edition | 23 May 2026, more than 51,000 letters, across 47 locations |
| Cumulative | About 12 lakh appointment letters across the editions held |

The cumulative figure is worth pausing on. The original target was 10 lakh recruitments, and roughly 12 lakh appointment letters have now been distributed, so the stated target has been passed. Editions have run at a rate of roughly three or four a year since launch, each typically covering 50,000 to 71,000 appointees at once, held simultaneously across dozens of locations with the Prime Minister joining by video conferencing.

## Which departments the recruits join

New appointees join 38 ministries and departments of the Government of India. The departments that recur most across editions are the ones with the largest workforces and the highest vacancy volumes.

| Department or ministry | Typical posts |
|---|---|
| Railways | Level 1 posts, technical staff, clerical grades |
| Home Affairs | Central armed police forces, administrative staff |
| Posts | Postal assistants, sorting assistants, postmen, gramin dak sevaks |
| Revenue | Income tax and customs staff, inspectors, tax assistants |
| Financial Services | Public sector bank and insurance staff |
| Health and Family Welfare | Paramedical, nursing and administrative staff |
| Higher Education | Teaching and non-teaching staff |
| Defence (civilian) | Civilian posts in defence establishments |

Appointments span every level of the central service: Group A, Group B Gazetted, Group B Non-Gazetted, and Group C. So the letters handed out at a single mela can cover anything from a directly recruited officer to a Group C clerical appointee.

## The routes that actually lead to a Rozgar Mela letter

Since Rozgar Mela is the destination rather than the door, the practical question is which examinations feed it. These are the main ones.

| Recruiting body | What it fills |
|---|---|
| Staff Selection Commission (SSC) | CGL, CHSL, MTS, GD Constable, JE, Stenographer, CPO |
| Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB) | Group D Level 1, ALP, Technician, NTPC, JE |
| UPSC | Civil Services, Engineering Services, CDS, CAPF, CMS and specialist posts |
| IBPS and SBI | Bank PO, Clerk, Specialist Officer and equivalent |
| Departmental recruitment | Ministry and department-specific posts |

If you want to be one of the people receiving a letter, that table is where to look. Our pages on the [RRB Group D](/sarkari-naukri/rrb-group-d-2026) recruitment, currently at the exam stage, and [SSC CGL](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-cgl-2026) cover two of the highest-volume routes in detail.

Notice what this means for timing. Someone receiving a letter at a mela in 2026 typically applied a year or more earlier, sat one or two examinations, cleared a physical or skill test where applicable, passed document verification and cleared a medical. The mela is the visible end of a long and largely invisible process.

## Karmayogi Prarambh

Alongside the appointment letters, the government launched Karmayogi Prarambh, an online orientation course for new government appointees.

It runs on the iGOT Karmayogi platform, which carries more than 400 e-learning courses and is designed for access from any device. The orientation module covers what a new recruit needs at the start of government service: conduct rules, workplace ethics, the basics of the department they are joining, human resource policies, and general capacity building.

For a new appointee this is the practical first step after the letter arrives, and it is worth taking seriously rather than clicking through. Government service has procedural expectations that are rarely spelled out again after induction.

## Three different things people confuse

A large share of the confusion around this subject comes from three unrelated things sharing similar names. They are worth separating clearly.

| | What it is | Can you apply? |
|---|---|---|
| PM's Rozgar Mela | Ceremony where the PM distributes appointment letters to already-selected central government recruits | No. There is no form |
| State or district rozgar mela | Local job fair run by an employment exchange or district administration, where private and some public employers interview candidates on the spot | Yes. Attend in person, usually with free registration at the venue or on the state employment portal |
| PMRY, the old Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana | A self-employment scheme from 1993 providing subsidised credit to set up small enterprises, since subsumed into later programmes | No. It is discontinued as a standalone scheme |

The middle one is the source of most of the misunderstanding, and it is also genuinely useful. District employment exchanges and state skill development departments run job fairs, often called rozgar melas, where employers conduct walk-in interviews. Those are real events you can attend, they do have registration, and they mostly offer private sector and contractual roles rather than permanent government posts. They are not the Prime Minister's Rozgar Mela.

If you are looking for the self-employment and credit route that PMRY once served, the current equivalents are the [PM Mudra loan scheme](/sarkari-yojana/pm-mudra-loan-yojana-2026) for small business credit and the [PMFME scheme](/sarkari-yojana/pmfme-scheme-2026) for micro food processing enterprises, both of which do have application processes.

## Why the confusion exists at all

It is worth understanding why so many people search for a Rozgar Mela application, because the reason is not stupidity on their part.

The name invites it. A mela is an event people attend, and rozgar means employment, so "employment fair" is a reasonable reading of the words. District employment exchanges have run genuine job fairs under exactly that name for decades, so the term already meant something attendable long before 2022.

The coverage invites it too. Reporting on each edition leads with a large number of jobs and appointment letters, which reads to a job seeker as an opportunity being announced rather than as the conclusion of recruitments that closed a year or more earlier.

And the gap gets filled by sites that profit from the traffic. A search for a form that does not exist still produces pages offering one, because there is advertising revenue in ranking for a high-volume query regardless of whether the answer is real.

None of that is the searcher's fault. The correct response is simply to know what the initiative is, and to redirect the effort towards the examinations that actually lead to these posts.

## How to spot the fake registration pages

Sites publishing Rozgar Mela registration forms are either confusing it with a district job fair or, in the worst cases, collecting personal data on the strength of a job promise. A few checks protect you.

There is no fee for any central government recruitment beyond the official examination fee paid on the recruiting body's own portal. Nobody collects a registration fee for a Rozgar Mela.

Central recruitment happens on official portals: ssc.gov.in, upsc.gov.in, rrbapply.gov.in, ibps.in and the individual department sites. A form hosted on a blog or a private site is not a government application.

An appointment letter follows an examination and a selection process. Any offer of a government appointment letter without an examination is not genuine.

Be careful with what you share. Aadhaar numbers, bank details and document scans handed to an unofficial "registration" site are the actual product being collected.

## A realistic path to a central government job

Since the honest answer to "how do I get a Rozgar Mela letter" is "clear a recruitment examination", it is worth setting out what that path actually looks like rather than leaving it abstract.

Start by matching your qualification to the right examinations, because applying to things you are not eligible for wastes application fees and months.

| Your qualification | Examinations to target |
|---|---|
| Class 10 | RRB Group D, SSC MTS, India Post GDS, Home Ministry Group C posts |
| Class 12 | SSC CHSL, SSC GD Constable, RRB NTPC undergraduate posts, IB Security Assistant |
| ITI or diploma | RRB ALP, RRB Technician, SSC Junior Engineer, technical posts in defence establishments |
| Graduation | SSC CGL, RRB NTPC graduate posts, IBPS PO and Clerk, UPSC examinations |

Then work on the base that these examinations share. Quantitative aptitude, reasoning, general awareness and English recur across almost all of them, so preparation compounds across applications rather than being spent on one attempt. The subject-specific or trade-specific portion is what changes.

Apply broadly and continuously. The single biggest difference between candidates who get in and candidates who do not is often not ability but application volume: many aspirants apply to two or three examinations a year when they were eligible for eight or ten. Application windows are short, typically about a month, and there is no penalty for applying to several.

Track the official portals directly rather than through aggregators. Notifications, corrigenda and date changes appear on ssc.gov.in, rrbapply.gov.in, upsc.gov.in and ibps.in before they reach secondary sites.

Finally, plan for the full timeline. From application to appointment letter commonly runs 12 to 24 months across the examination stages, document verification and medical. Someone receiving a letter at a mela today applied a long time ago, and that is the horizon to plan against.

## Does Rozgar Mela create new jobs?

Worth addressing directly, since it is the most common critical question.

Rozgar Mela is a filling exercise rather than a job creation programme. The posts handed out are existing sanctioned vacancies in ministries and departments, and the initiative directs those departments to fill them in mission mode rather than letting them sit vacant. So the effect is on the speed and visibility of recruitment against posts that already exist on paper, not on the creation of new posts.

That is a real effect and not a trivial one. Sanctioned vacancies in central departments have historically been slow to fill, and a coordinated push with a public deadline changes departmental behaviour. But a candidate should understand the mechanism accurately: the vacancies advertised by SSC, RRB, UPSC and the banks are the same vacancies whose appointment letters appear at these events.

## What happens between selection and the letter

Candidates who have cleared an examination often assume the appointment letter follows within weeks, and the gap surprises them. The intervening steps are worth knowing.

After the final result, the recruiting body prepares a merit list and allocates candidates to departments, zones or regions based on merit and the preferences submitted during the application. Document verification follows, where originals are checked against everything claimed in the application, including category, age relaxation and educational qualification. A medical examination applies where the post carries a medical standard. Police verification and character antecedent checks are then carried out by the appointing department.

Only after all of that does the appointing department issue the appointment letter, and that is the document handed over at a Rozgar Mela or sent directly.

Two practical consequences follow. Keep every original document safe and accessible from the moment you apply, since the verification can come many months later and a missing certificate at that stage is a serious problem. And keep the contact details in your application current, because departments communicate through the email and mobile number on record, and candidates do lose appointments by missing communications sent to a number they stopped using.

## What this means for you

If you already have a central government appointment letter from a Rozgar Mela, complete the Karmayogi Prarambh module, report as instructed in your letter, and keep every document from your recruitment process.

If you want one, apply through the recruiting bodies. Track ssc.gov.in, rrbapply.gov.in, upsc.gov.in and ibps.in, apply to everything you qualify for rather than waiting for the perfect match, and start preparation before a notification appears rather than after, since application windows typically run a month and exam dates follow within a few months.

And if a site asks you to register for Rozgar Mela, close it.

## Frequently asked questions

**How do I apply for PM Rozgar Mela 2026?**
You cannot. Rozgar Mela has no application form, no registration, no eligibility criteria and no last date. It is the event at which the Prime Minister distributes appointment letters to people who have already been selected through normal recruitment processes such as SSC, UPSC, RRB, IBPS or departmental examinations. Any site offering a Rozgar Mela registration form is describing something that does not exist.

**What is the PM Rozgar Mela scheme?**
Rozgar Mela is a central government recruitment drive launched on 22 October 2022 with a target of appointing 10 lakh personnel in mission mode. Under it, ministries and departments fill existing sanctioned vacancies on an accelerated timeline, and the Prime Minister distributes appointment letters to batches of new appointees at events held simultaneously across many locations via video conferencing.

**How many appointment letters has Rozgar Mela given out?**
About 12 lakh appointment letters have been distributed across the editions held since launch, which means the original target of 10 lakh has been passed. The 18th edition on 24 January 2026 covered more than 61,000 appointees, and the 19th edition on 23 May 2026 covered more than 51,000 across 47 locations.

**Is Rozgar Mela a real government scheme or a scam?**
The Rozgar Mela itself is genuine, run by the Government of India with appointment letters distributed by the Prime Minister. The scams are the third-party websites offering Rozgar Mela registration, application forms or guaranteed appointment letters, since no such process exists. Never pay a fee or share Aadhaar and bank details with any site claiming to register you for it.

**Which exams lead to a Rozgar Mela appointment letter?**
The normal central recruitment examinations: Staff Selection Commission examinations such as CGL, CHSL, MTS and GD Constable; Railway Recruitment Board recruitments such as Group D, ALP, Technician and NTPC; UPSC examinations; IBPS and SBI bank examinations; and departmental recruitments. Clearing one of these, along with any skill test, document verification and medical, is what results in the appointment letter handed over at a mela.

**Which departments recruit through Rozgar Mela?**
New appointees join 38 ministries and departments of the Government of India. The ones appearing most often are Railways, Home Affairs, Posts, Revenue, Financial Services, Health and Family Welfare, Higher Education and civilian posts in Defence. Appointments cover Group A, Group B Gazetted, Group B Non-Gazetted and Group C levels.

**What is Karmayogi Prarambh?**
Karmayogi Prarambh is an online orientation course for newly appointed government employees, launched alongside Rozgar Mela and hosted on the iGOT Karmayogi platform, which carries more than 400 e-learning courses accessible from any device. It covers conduct rules, workplace ethics, departmental basics and human resource policies for people beginning government service.

**Does Rozgar Mela create new government jobs?**
No. It fills existing sanctioned vacancies in ministries and departments rather than creating new posts. Its effect is on the speed and coordination of recruitment against posts that already exist, by directing departments to fill them in mission mode. The vacancies advertised by SSC, RRB, UPSC and the banks are the same vacancies whose appointment letters are handed out at these events.

**Is the district rozgar mela the same as the PM Rozgar Mela?**
No, and this is the most common confusion. District and state rozgar melas are job fairs organised by employment exchanges or district administrations, where employers conduct walk-in interviews and candidates can register and attend in person. They mostly offer private sector and contractual roles. The Prime Minister's Rozgar Mela is a ceremony for distributing central government appointment letters to people already selected, with no attendance or registration for the public.

**What is the difference between Rozgar Mela and PMRY?**
They are unrelated. Rozgar Mela, launched in 2022, is a central government recruitment drive and appointment letter distribution initiative. PMRY, the Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana of 1993, was a self-employment scheme providing subsidised credit to help people set up small enterprises, and it has since been subsumed into later programmes. For self-employment credit today, the PM Mudra loan scheme and PMFME are the current routes.

**When is the next Rozgar Mela?**
No fixed calendar is published in advance. Editions have been held at a rate of roughly three or four a year since October 2022, with the 19th held on 23 May 2026. Dates are announced by the Prime Minister's Office shortly before each event. Since there is nothing for a member of the public to apply to, the date matters only to candidates who have already been selected and will be informed by their recruiting department.

**I got selected in SSC. Will I get my letter at a Rozgar Mela?**
Possibly, depending on whether your department includes your batch in an upcoming edition. Appointment letters for central government posts are issued by the appointing department, and some batches are handed over at a Rozgar Mela event while others are issued directly. Either way the letter is the same, and your recruiting department will inform you of the arrangements. There is nothing you need to do to be included.

description: Telangana Rs 500 gas cylinder scheme 2026 guide: Mahalakshmi LPG eligibility, DBT process, PMUY stacking, 42.9 lakh beneficiaries, apply via MeeSeva now.
content:
## Telangana Rs 500 gas cylinder scheme 2026 at a glance

The Telangana Rs 500 gas cylinder scheme lets white ration card families buy a 14.2 kg domestic LPG refill for a flat Rs 500, with the state government reimbursing the balance directly to the woman applicant's bank account. It runs under the wider Mahalakshmi umbrella of the Congress government's six poll guarantees, alongside Rs 2,500 monthly DBT to women and free TSRTC bus travel. The scheme is often called Mahalakshmi LPG in official communication and in banking transaction narrations.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy formally rolled out the cylinder benefit on 27 February 2024 from LB Stadium in Hyderabad, three months after the government took charge. Enrolment for the first tranche happened through the PrajaPalana campaign, where families that already held a white ration card were auto-mapped to the LPG rolls without a fresh application. Later applicants use MeeSeva centres or the PrajaPalana portal to add themselves.

As of Telangana Formation Day 2026, 42.9 lakh families are drawing cylinders at Rs 500, per Sakshi Post's June 2026 reporting. The eligible universe is 89.99 lakh white ration card households out of about 1.20 crore total LPG connections in the state, which means the scheme has reached roughly 48 percent of the pool it was designed for. Broader Mahalakshmi enrolment across all three components sits at 1.28 crore women, per schemesinindia.in's July 2026 tracker.

## How the Rs 500 mechanism actually works

The Rs 500 rate isn't a discounted price at the delivery point. The beneficiary still pays the full retail rate to the LPG distributor, then gets a reimbursement from the state treasury within 48 hours. In Hyderabad, the IOCL 14.2 kg domestic refill sat at Rs 903 in July 2026, so a Mahalakshmi-registered woman pays Rs 903 upfront and receives Rs 403 back through DBT to her Aadhaar-linked account. Her net out-of-pocket cost is Rs 500 per cylinder.

The state runs a monthly advance settlement with IOCL, BPCL and HPCL, so there are no OMC arrears eating into the delivery pipeline. This matters because earlier subsidy models in other states collapsed when the state government fell behind on reimbursements and distributors quietly stopped delivering. Telangana's civil supplies department pre-pays the oil companies before the delivery month begins, and the woman's DBT clears against her own bank account, not the distributor's.

The distributor issues a standard IOCL, BPCL or HPCL bill in the customer's name. That bill is the trigger. The oil company's back-end shares the delivery record with Telangana Civil Supplies, the department cross-checks against the Mahalakshmi enrolment list, and the DBT is released. If the delivery record hits by Monday, the money typically shows up by Wednesday in most Hyderabad and Ranga Reddy circles, per household reports collated by Deccan Chronicle in April 2026.

Bank account rules matter here. The DBT lands only in the account that's Aadhaar-linked and mapped to the LPG connection in the applicant woman's name. If the connection is in the husband's name, the reimbursement won't release. Households in that situation have to transfer the connection to the woman first, using KYC at the distributor with the ration card and Aadhaar as proof.

## Worked example: Warangal BPL family, 8 refills a year

Sarala from Hanamkonda in Warangal district holds a white ration card issued in 2019 and an IOCL connection registered in her name since 2021. Her family of four uses about 8 refills a year, which is close to the Telangana average for a household with two adults and two school-going children. Before Mahalakshmi, she paid the full IOCL rate every time and received the central Rs 300 DBT subsidy only if she was a PMUY beneficiary, which she wasn't.

From March 2024, Sarala's math changed. She still pays Rs 903 per refill at the door. Within 48 hours, Rs 403 lands in her SBI account. Over 8 refills a year, her total out-of-pocket cost drops from Rs 7,224 to Rs 4,000, a saving of Rs 3,224 across the year. If she was also on PMUY (which she isn't, but many Telangana women are), her net cost would drop further because the central Rs 300 subsidy would stack on top.

Multiply Sarala's saving across the 42.9 lakh active beneficiaries the state reported in June 2026, and the annual state outflow works out to roughly Rs 13,830 crore at 8 refills per household. That's a big line item, which is why the Deccan Chronicle "letter of promise" episode (covered below) mattered so much politically.

## Eligibility: white ration card and the four exclusions

Only white ration card households qualify. White cards are Telangana's Below Poverty Line category, distinct from pink (Antyodaya) and grey (Above Poverty Line, no PDS benefits). If a family's ration card is anything other than white, the Mahalakshmi LPG benefit doesn't release, even if the woman applies.

The connection must be in the name of the woman applicant. One connection per family is enrolled. If a family holds two LPG connections (which is rare but happens in joint families with separate cooking arrangements), only the primary connection linked to the ration card gets the Rs 500 rate.

Aadhaar linkage is non-negotiable. The applicant's Aadhaar must be seeded into both the LPG customer record at the distributor and the bank account where the DBT lands. Any mismatch (say, Aadhaar-linked to Bank A but LPG-linked to Bank B) will hold up the transfer until KYC is refreshed.

Four exclusions cut the pool down from the 1.20 crore total LPG connections in Telangana to the eligible 89.99 lakh white-card households. Government employees are excluded, on the standard logic that they draw regular salaries and pension. Income tax payers filing returns above the taxable slab are out. GST-registered business owners are out, since the presumption is commercial income. Households owning a four-wheeler (not counting two-wheelers or tractors) are excluded, on the asset-test principle used across most Telangana welfare schemes.

## How to apply: MeeSeva, PrajaPalana, and auto-enrolment for existing ration holders

Most eligible families never had to apply. When the Congress government ran the PrajaPalana door-to-door enrolment campaign in December 2023 and January 2024, families holding an existing white ration card were mapped to Mahalakshmi automatically. The first Rs 500 cylinders started delivering from March 2024 without any extra paperwork for those households.

New applicants, or families whose auto-enrolment didn't complete, use one of two routes. The first is a MeeSeva centre visit. Any of the 4,500+ MeeSeva outlets across Telangana can accept the Mahalakshmi LPG application form, along with the ration card, Aadhaar, LPG consumer number and bank passbook. The MeeSeva operator uploads the record to the civil supplies backend, and the applicant gets an SMS acknowledgment on the registered mobile number.

The second route is the PrajaPalana portal at prajapalana.telangana.gov.in. Applicants log in with their ration card number and Aadhaar OTP, then add or update their LPG connection details. This route works best for households that already have a ration card mapped in the system and just need to link a new LPG connection.

Turnaround from application to first Rs 500 cylinder typically runs 15 to 30 days. Delays usually come from Aadhaar-bank mismatches or from LPG connections that are still in the husband's name.

## PMUY plus Mahalakshmi LPG: can you use both?

Yes, and this is the single biggest gap in the SERP for this query. Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) is a central government scheme that gives BPL women a free LPG connection (deposit and hose kit waived) plus a Rs 300 per cylinder subsidy for up to 12 refills a year, deposited directly to the woman's bank account. Mahalakshmi LPG is a Telangana state scheme on top of that.

For a PMUY beneficiary in Telangana who also holds a white ration card, the two subsidies stack. She pays Rs 903 at the door. She gets Rs 300 from the Centre under PMUY. She gets Rs 103 from the state under Mahalakshmi. Her net out-of-pocket cost lands at Rs 500. The state absorbs whatever residual gap exists between the PMUY reimbursement and the Rs 500 target price, which is why the state DBT amount varies across households depending on their PMUY status.

For a non-PMUY white-card holder, the state absorbs the full Rs 403 gap alone. Either way, the beneficiary's out-of-pocket cost is Rs 500 flat. The PMUY overlay just changes who's paying what share to the exchequer.

If a woman is PMUY-eligible but hasn't enrolled, she should enrol in PMUY separately through her LPG distributor. That reduces the state's per-cylinder outlay and makes her position more stable if state finances tighten. PMUY enrolment doesn't cost anything and doesn't disturb the Mahalakshmi entitlement.

## Cross-state comparison: Telangana vs Andhra Pradesh vs Karnataka vs PMUY central

Southern states have very different LPG welfare models. Telangana's is neither the cheapest per cylinder nor the most generous on refill volume, but it strikes a middle path that covers the widest pool.

| Scheme | State | Cost to beneficiary per cylinder | Refills covered per year | Eligibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mahalakshmi LPG | Telangana | Rs 500 | ~8 to 10 (usage based, capped at 3-year household average) | White ration card, one woman per family |
| Deepam-2 | Andhra Pradesh | Rs 0 (fully free) | 3 | All women residents, no BPL filter |
| Anila Bhagya | Karnataka | Rs 0 for first 5 refills | 5 | BPL, PMUY beneficiaries |
| PMUY (central) | All India | ~Rs 603 (Rs 903 minus Rs 300) | Up to 12 | BPL women registered under Ujjwala |

Andhra Pradesh's Deepam-2 is the most generous on price (fully free) but caps at 3 refills. For a 4-member household using 8 refills a year, the AP beneficiary pays full rate on 5 of them, so annual out-of-pocket ends up higher than a Telangana counterpart.

Karnataka's Anila Bhagya covers 5 refills at zero cost but is limited to PMUY beneficiaries. A BPL household in Karnataka that isn't PMUY-registered gets nothing.

Telangana's model runs longer on refills (matched to household consumption) and covers a much wider pool (all white-card holders, not just PMUY women). That's why the beneficiary count is 42.9 lakh, well above what a PMUY-only overlay would produce.

## Quota and the last-three-years consumption cap

The scheme is not open-ended on refill count. Telangana Civil Supplies caps each household's subsidised refills at the average of that household's last three years of LPG consumption. For a family that took 9 refills in each of 2021, 2022 and 2023, the subsidy applies to up to 9 refills a year going forward. Refills beyond that quota can still be bought, but at the full market rate with no state DBT.

For newly enrolled families with no three-year history (typically PMUY beneficiaries who took their first connection recently), the cap defaults to 8 refills a year in year one, with the actual usage building the baseline for subsequent years. This is the number Sarala's household in the worked example above sits at.

The cap keeps the scheme fiscally predictable and stops resale scenarios where a family buys many cylinders at Rs 500 and offloads them to commercial users at higher rates. Distributors also flag anomalies. A sudden jump from 8 refills a year to 15 triggers a review by the local civil supplies office.

## Status check and grievance

Two portals cover the routine status questions. The Telangana EPDS portal at epds.telangana.gov.in shows the ration card status, the Mahalakshmi mapping, and the last DBT release against a given LPG connection. Households log in with their ration card number or Aadhaar-registered mobile.

The Telangana Civil Supplies portal at civilsupplies.telangana.gov.in carries the department-level circulars, the current subsidy per district, and the monthly beneficiary count. The CMO Telangana site at cmo.telangana.gov.in is a secondary reference for scheme policy announcements, not for individual status.

For grievances (DBT not received after 48 hours, LPG connection not linked, Aadhaar mismatch), the toll-free helpline is 1800-425-5888. It runs from 8 AM to 8 PM on all working days. MeeSeva centres also accept written grievances and forward them to the district civil supplies officer.

Distributor-level issues (delivery refused, bill not raised) go to the LPG distributor first, then to the oil company customer care (IOCL 1906, BPCL 1800-224-344, HPCL 1800-2333-555) if the distributor doesn't resolve within 48 hours.

## What changed in 2026: 42.9 lakh beneficiaries and the letter of promise

The scheme's biggest 2026 wobble came in April, when a state budget dispute triggered a brief speculation that Mahalakshmi LPG reimbursements might be paused. Deccan Chronicle reported on 12 April 2026 that Civil Supplies Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy issued a "letter of promise" to OMCs, guaranteeing continued monthly advance settlements through the 2026-27 financial year. The letter cleared the immediate uncertainty and deliveries continued without interruption.

Beneficiary numbers climbed steadily through the year. From 38.2 lakh active families in March 2025, the count hit 42.9 lakh by June 2026, per Sakshi Post's Formation Day reporting. Broader Mahalakshmi enrolment across the DBT-to-women and free-bus-travel components combined reached 1.28 crore, per schemesinindia.in's July 2026 tracker.

The state's monthly outlay on the LPG component alone runs to roughly Rs 1,150 crore, based on 42.9 lakh families at an average subsidy of Rs 403 across an average of 0.66 refills per household per month. That's a durable expenditure line the state has been carrying without visible arrears, which is why the April letter of promise held.

Enrolment additions have slowed since the initial PrajaPalana surge. Most eligible white-card holders were auto-mapped in the first six months. New additions now come mostly from newlywed women getting fresh LPG connections in their own name, and from families that upgraded from grey to white ration card after income verification.

## Documents required

Applicants at a MeeSeva centre or on the PrajaPalana portal need the following documents in hand.

A valid Telangana white ration card, current and not marked as inactive on the EPDS portal. The card must have the woman applicant listed as head of family or as an adult member.

The LPG connection consumer number, printed on the top of any recent gas bill or the SV/SC number card issued by the distributor. This has to match a connection registered in the applicant's name.

Aadhaar card of the applicant, with the mobile number linked. OTP verification runs during application submission on the PrajaPalana portal.

Bank passbook or a cancelled cheque showing the account number, IFSC code and the account holder's name (the applicant woman). The account must be Aadhaar-seeded, which the applicant can verify with any bank branch or through the UIDAI website's "Check Aadhaar and Bank Account Linking Status" tool.

Mobile number active on the applicant's name (for OTP and SMS acknowledgment). If the SIM is registered to a family member, the applicant should update KYC at the distributor to avoid delivery notification issues.

Passport-size photograph of the applicant (needed only at MeeSeva route, not online).

## Frequently asked questions

### Who qualifies for the Rs 500 gas cylinder in Telangana?

Telangana residents holding a white ration card qualify, with one woman per family designated as the applicant. The LPG connection must be in her name and Aadhaar-linked to her bank account. Government employees, income tax payers, GST-registered business owners and four-wheeler owners are excluded.

### How much money comes back to my bank account after buying a cylinder?

You pay the full IOCL, BPCL or HPCL retail rate at delivery. Within 48 hours, the state DBT transfers the gap between that retail rate and Rs 500 into your Aadhaar-linked account. In Hyderabad at the July 2026 rate of Rs 903, the DBT is Rs 403.

### Do I need to apply separately or was I auto-enrolled?

Families that held a Telangana white ration card during the PrajaPalana campaign in December 2023 or January 2024 were auto-enrolled without a fresh application. Anyone who missed that or got a white card after February 2024 applies through a MeeSeva centre or the PrajaPalana portal at prajapalana.telangana.gov.in.

### Can I use PMUY and Mahalakshmi LPG together?

Yes. PMUY gives you a Rs 300 per cylinder central subsidy for up to 12 refills a year. Mahalakshmi tops that up with a state DBT so your net cost lands at Rs 500 flat. The two subsidies stack, and PMUY enrolment doesn't disturb your Mahalakshmi entitlement.

### How many cylinders can I get at Rs 500 in a year?

The cap is set at your household's average LPG consumption across the last three years. For a family with a 9-refill annual average, all 9 refills a year get the Rs 500 rate. New PMUY beneficiaries with no three-year history default to 8 refills in year one. Refills beyond the cap are available at full market rate.

### Why hasn't the DBT amount landed in my account?

Common reasons are Aadhaar not seeded to your bank account, LPG connection registered in your husband's name instead of yours, mobile number KYC mismatch at the distributor, or a delay in the oil company sharing the delivery record with civil supplies. Check the EPDS portal for your Mahalakshmi status, or call 1800-425-5888.

### Is the scheme still running in 2026 after the budget dispute?

Yes. Civil Supplies Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy issued a written commitment to oil marketing companies in April 2026, guaranteeing monthly advance settlements through the 2026-27 financial year. Deliveries continued without interruption, and the 42.9 lakh beneficiary count as of June 2026 is up from 38.2 lakh a year earlier.

### What if my ration card is pink or grey, not white?

Pink Antyodaya card holders get separate PDS benefits but Mahalakshmi LPG isn't one of them. Grey card holders are Above Poverty Line and don't qualify for either. If your family income has dropped and you should now hold a white card, apply for card conversion at a MeeSeva centre with income and residence proof.

### Does the connection have to be in the woman's name?

Yes. The DBT will only release to an Aadhaar-linked account that matches the LPG customer record. If your existing connection is in your husband's name, you can transfer it to your name at the distributor with a KYC form, both spouses' Aadhaar cards, and the ration card. Transfer typically completes in 7 to 15 days.

### How do I check my payment status online?

Log in to the EPDS Telangana portal at epds.telangana.gov.in using your ration card number and Aadhaar OTP. The Mahalakshmi tab shows enrolment status, and the DBT history section lists each transfer with date and amount. The Telangana Civil Supplies site at civilsupplies.telangana.gov.in carries department circulars if you want the policy-level view.

### Can I get the benefit if I moved to Telangana from another state?

You need a Telangana-issued white ration card, which requires proof of residence in the state. There's no minimum-years-of-residence rule for the ration card itself, but you'll need address proof at the MeeSeva application step. Once the white card is issued, Mahalakshmi enrolment follows the same route as any other Telangana resident.

### What's the difference between Mahalakshmi LPG and Andhra Pradesh's Deepam-2?

Deepam-2 in AP gives 3 fully free cylinders a year to all women residents with no BPL filter. Mahalakshmi LPG in Telangana charges Rs 500 per cylinder but covers 8 to 10 refills a year based on household usage, limited to white ration card families. Telangana's model works out cheaper annually for medium-usage families and covers a wider refill count.
