description: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao 2026: 11-year status, Haryana SRB drop to 898, Union Budget 2026-27 Rs. 28,183 cr MWCD line, plus SSY convergence and district data.
content:
## What Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is in 2026

Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is a national programme launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Panipat, Haryana on 22 January 2015 to arrest India's declining Child Sex Ratio, protect the girl child, and improve girls' access to education. In January 2026, the programme entered its 11th year as a component of the Sambal sub-scheme under the umbrella Mission Shakti, jointly implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the Ministry of Education.

Per the Ministry of Women and Child Development's decade-review release (PIB PRID 2094929, 21 January 2025), the national Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) improved from 918 girls per 1,000 boys in FY 2014-15 to 930 in FY 2023-24, a 12-point gain. Girls' Gross Enrolment Ratio in secondary education rose from 75.51% to 78% over the same window, and institutional deliveries rose from 61% to 97.3%. These are the headline BBBP metrics that most competitor pages continue to cite as of July 2026.

BBBP is not a cash-transfer scheme. There is no individual application form, and no eligible family receives Rs. 1 lakh or Rs. 2,100 or a "free laptop" from the government under this scheme. Multiple websites currently offering "BBBP application" or "BBBP laptop" are scams; the Ministry of Women and Child Development has issued a public fact-check confirming this. Financial support to the girl child is delivered through the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY), a separate small-savings scheme launched alongside BBBP on the same day.

The programme sits inside the broader Mission Shakti (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 cycle), which the Union Budget 2026-27 funds with an overall Ministry of Women and Child Development allocation of Rs. 28,183 crore, up 15.6% year-on-year (Demand No. 101, indiabudget.gov.in). Continuation guidelines for Mission Shakti beyond 31 March 2026 have not been published as of the date of this article.

---

## The 11-year status check as of July 2026

Two developments in FY 2025-26 have materially changed the BBBP conversation.

**The 11th anniversary of BBBP (22 January 2026)** was observed by the Ministry of Women and Child Development at the National Girl Child Day event. The observance emphasised the shift from awareness-only interventions to enforcement plus skilling convergence, particularly the Non-Traditional Livelihoods (NTL) skilling module introduced in 2022 for adolescent girls in STEM, aviation, defence, and construction sectors.

**Haryana's Sex Ratio at Birth fell to 898 girls per 1,000 boys in January-April 2026**, per Civil Registration System data reported by ThePrint on 15 May 2026, down from a 2019 peak of 923 and from a 2025 full-year figure of 923. The district-level collapse is more striking: Charkhi Dadri 768, Ambala 843, Mahendragarh 847, Fatehabad 893, all for the Jan-Apr 2026 window. The Nayab Singh Saini state government has activated a multi-community outreach involving pandits, maulvis, and granthis to embed anti-female-foeticide messaging in religious sermons, alongside 218 inter-state raids in 2025 under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PC-PNDT) Act. Since 2015, Haryana has filed 1,375 FIRs under PC-PNDT and Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Acts.

These two datapoints frame the broader question the 11-year mark has raised: after Rs. 928 crore Phase 1 (2015-2020) and pan-India expansion in 2018, why is the flagship worst-affected state losing ground again? The next sections walk through what BBBP actually does, its funding architecture, and where current interventions are and are not working.

---

## BBBP timeline: 100 districts in 2015 to 640 plus and Mission Shakti convergence

BBBP has evolved substantially since launch. The timeline table below is anchored to primary Ministry of Women and Child Development and PIB sources.

| Year | Milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 22 Jan 2015 | PM Modi launched BBBP at Panipat, Haryana with initial Rs. 100 crore outlay, targeting 100 low-CSR districts | PIB, Jan 2015 |
| 8 Mar 2018 | Pan-India expansion announced covering all districts | PIB, Mar 2018 |
| Phase 1 close (2020) | Rs. 928 crore total Phase 1 allocation, roughly 58% utilised | CAG Report 2017 + PIB |
| 2021-22 | BBBP subsumed into Mission Shakti's Sambal sub-scheme, 100% centrally funded | Mission Shakti Operational Guidelines |
| 2022 | Non-Traditional Livelihoods (NTL) skilling module added for adolescent girls in STEM, defence sectors | Ministry of Women and Child Development |
| 21 Jan 2025 | 10-year decade review release, national SRB gain 918 to 930 | PIB PRID 2094929 |
| 22 Jan 2026 | 11th anniversary, 640 plus districts covered, SSY at 4.53 crore accounts | PIB anniversary note Jan 2026 |
| 15 May 2026 | ThePrint report: Haryana SRB collapse to 898 (Jan-Apr 2026) | ThePrint |

The 2021 merge into Mission Shakti moved BBBP from a standalone campaign to a permanent line-item under the ministry's umbrella women-safety programme, alongside One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181, and Nari Adalat under Sambal. The other Mission Shakti vertical, Samarthya, houses PMMVY (Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana), Palna creches, and Sakhi Niwas working-women's hostels.

---

## Sex Ratio at Birth: what the numbers say in 2026

India's national Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) improved from 918 to 930 girls per 1,000 boys between FY 2014-15 and FY 2023-24, per Ministry of Women and Child Development (PIB PRID 2094929, 21 Jan 2025). State-level performance is uneven, and 2026 data suggests some states are regressing.

Latest available state-wise SRB snapshot:

| State/UT | SRB (girls per 1,000 boys) | Data year | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| India national | 930 | 2023-24 | Ministry of Women and Child Development, PIB PRID 2094929 |
| Haryana | 898 (Jan-Apr 2026) | 2026 partial | Civil Registration System via ThePrint 15 May 2026 |
| Bihar | 891 | 2022 | SRS |
| Rajasthan | 891 | 2022 | SRS |
| Punjab | 904 | 2022 | SRS |
| Uttar Pradesh | 906 | 2022 | SRS |
| Kerala | 951 | 2022 | SRS |
| Nagaland | 1,068 | 2022 | SRS |

The national figure is aggregated across 36 states and UTs and hides significant variation. States with strong intervention coverage (Kerala, Nagaland) hold above 950. States with historic son-preference (Haryana, Bihar, Rajasthan) hover in the 890-910 band with fluctuation year to year. The FY 2020-21 NFHS-5 round put India's SRB at 929 (against 919 in NFHS-4), which independently corroborates the direction of the CRS-based national trend.

The 2026 Haryana partial data (898) is the sharpest downward move in a decade for the state that hosts the programme's ceremonial launch point (Panipat). Independent analysts have flagged three drivers: (a) enforcement fatigue in local PC-PNDT machinery, (b) migration-linked ultrasound cross-border shopping, and (c) a shift of son-preference behaviour to second and third-order births as first-born-girl selective abortion has been curtailed. The full-year 2026 figure will be released by CRS Haryana in Q2 FY 2027-28.

---

## Haryana 2026: SRB drop and what the state is doing

Haryana's SRB drop is the biggest 2026 story on BBBP. The Nayab Singh Saini state government has activated a multi-pronged response since May 2026 that other states with declining SRB (Bihar, Rajasthan) will likely watch.

The response has four components:

- **Religious-community outreach:** the state has drafted pandits, maulvis, and granthis to embed anti-female-foeticide messaging in Sunday sermons, Friday khutbas, and gurdwara diwans.
- **PC-PNDT enforcement scale-up:** 218 inter-state raids in 2025 alone, targeting cross-border ultrasound tourism to neighbouring Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Punjab.
- **District-level review:** the 11 districts where SRB has dropped over 20 points get monthly DM-chaired task-force meetings with WCD, Health, Education, and Police coordinating.
- **NTL scholarship expansion:** Non-Traditional Livelihoods scholarship extended to girl children in the 11 worst-affected districts.

Since 2015, Haryana has filed 1,375 FIRs under the PC-PNDT Act and the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act. Roughly 12% have resulted in convictions, with the balance in trial or under investigation. The state government has requested the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to fast-track PC-PNDT special-court establishment in the 11 worst-affected districts.

For a family in Haryana, the practical shift in 2026 is heightened surveillance on ultrasound clinic prescriptions, mandatory Form F recordkeeping for every scan, and increased spot-checks on both registered clinics and mobile ultrasound units. Sex determination remains a criminal offence with up to 3 years imprisonment for the ultrasonographer and up to 5 years for repeat offenders.

---

## BBBP inside Mission Shakti: Sambal and Samarthya explained

Since FY 2021-22, BBBP has been a component of the Sambal sub-scheme within the umbrella Mission Shakti. Understanding the two sub-scheme structure clarifies where BBBP funds sit, what other programmes share the wallet, and what continuation looks like post the FY 2021-26 cycle end.

| Attribute | Sambal sub-scheme | Samarthya sub-scheme |
|---|---|---|
| Focus | Women safety and girl-child protection | Women empowerment, maternity, childcare |
| Components | BBBP, One Stop Centres (OSC), Women Helpline 181, Nari Adalat | PMMVY (Matru Vandana Yojana), Sakhi Niwas working-women hostels, Palna creches, National Creche Scheme |
| Central funding share | 100% for BBBP; OSC and WHL funded from Nirbhaya Fund | 60:40 central:state for most components |
| FY 2025-26 allocation | Rs. 629 crore (per PIB PRID 2080711) | Rs. 2,521 crore (per PIB PRID 2080711) |
| Total Mission Shakti FY 2025-26 | Rs. 3,150 crore | (same) |

The FY 2021-26 Mission Shakti cycle ends on 31 March 2026. As of the date of this article, the Ministry of Women and Child Development has not published continuation guidelines beyond that date. The Union Budget 2026-27 signalled continued funding through the overall MWCD allocation increase (Rs. 28,183 crore, 15.6% up year-on-year), but the specific sub-scheme-level allocation for FY 2026-27 requires reading the Statement of Budget Estimates (SBE-101, indiabudget.gov.in) directly and awaits confirmation from PRS India's Budget analysis.

Practically, this uncertainty is unlikely to disrupt BBBP field operations in 2026 because Sambal is 100% centrally funded and the ministry has committed to Mission Shakti continuation in Budget speeches. The open question is only whether the vertical structure remains the same or gets renamed for the 16th Finance Commission cycle.

---

## Union Budget 2026-27: what BBBP and Mission Shakti got

The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated Rs. 28,183 crore to the Ministry of Women and Child Development, a 15.6% increase over FY 2025-26, per the Demand for Grants (Demand No. 101, indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe101.pdf).

| Line item | FY 2026-27 BE (Rs. crore) | Change vs FY 2025-26 |
|---|---|---|
| MWCD total | 28,183 | +15.6% |
| Saksham Anganwadi + POSHAN 2.0 | 23,100 | Increased |
| One Stop Centres + Women Helpline (Sambal) | 405 (from Nirbhaya Fund) | Up from Rs. 240 crore RE FY 2025-26 |
| Standalone Mission Shakti (Sambal + Samarthya) FY 2026-27 line | Requires SBE-101 direct read; PRS India analysis pending | Increase confirmed in Budget speech |

The Rs. 405 crore allocation for One Stop Centres and Women Helpline signals continued expansion of frontline women-safety infrastructure, which sits alongside BBBP within the Sambal vertical. New OSC facilities are targeted for tier-2 and tier-3 districts under the FY 2026-27 push.

For BBBP specifically, the district-level intervention budget continues to flow through the 640 plus notified BBBP districts via State Nodal Officers, with the district magistrate chairing the multi-sector task force. Media and publicity expenditure (which had drawn the CAG critique in 2017) is now capped at 30% of the district envelope; the balance goes to enforcement, Anganwadi-school linkage, and ASHA/AWW training.

---

## Convergence with Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana

Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) is the financial-instrument counterpart to BBBP's advocacy work. Launched alongside BBBP on 22 January 2015, SSY is a small-savings scheme in the girl child's name that offers 8.2% tax-free interest (Section 80C eligible), with maturity when the girl turns 21.

Per PIB (PRID 2216748), SSY had 4.53 crore accounts opened as of December 2025, with total deposits crossing Rs. 3.33 lakh crore. The scheme is offered by all public sector banks, several private banks (SBI, PNB, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, BoB, and others), and the entire India Post network.

Key SSY parameters as of July 2026:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Interest rate (Jul-Sep 2026) | 8.2% per annum, compounded annually |
| Minimum annual deposit | Rs. 250 |
| Maximum annual deposit | Rs. 1.5 lakh |
| Deposit tenure | 15 years from account opening |
| Maturity | 21 years from opening (or on marriage after age 18, whichever earlier) |
| Tax status | EEE (exempt on contribution, interest, and maturity) under Section 80C |
| Eligibility | Girl child aged 0 to 10 years at account opening |
| Accounts per family | Maximum 2 girls (3 if second birth is twins) |

An SSY account opened at girl-child age 5 with the maximum Rs. 1.5 lakh annual deposit for 15 years generates approximately Rs. 69 lakh at maturity (age 21), assuming interest stays around 8%. This is why the BBBP plus SSY combination is the most-recommended vehicle for girl-child financial planning in India in 2026.

---

## How BBBP funds are used at the district level

BBBP is 100% centrally funded under Mission Shakti's Sambal vertical, disbursed to states via a State Nodal Officer and to districts via the district magistrate.

Standard BBBP district-level interventions:

1. **Community awareness.** Wall paintings, folk theatre (nukkad natak), radio jingles in the local language, mass wedding ceremonies for BPL girl-child families, mother-daughter meets at Anganwadi centres.
2. **PC-PNDT enforcement.** Ultrasound clinic Form F audits, sting operations on suspected sex-determination clinics, PNDT tribunal case follow-up.
3. **Girls' education outreach.** Enrolment drives at government schools, monitoring of girl-child dropout rates in secondary school (target: reduce by 5% annually), scholarship linkage to central and state schemes.
4. **ASHA and AWW training.** Village-level frontline worker training on Anti-Trafficking, Child Marriage Prohibition Act, POCSO, and adolescent reproductive health.
5. **NTL skilling (since 2022).** Non-Traditional Livelihoods skilling module for adolescent girls (ages 14 to 18) in STEM, aviation, defence, and construction sectors. This is the newest addition to the BBBP intervention set.
6. **Convergence camps.** Monthly camps linking BBBP-registered families to SSY account opening, immunisation, birth registration, and Aadhaar enrolment.

The average per-district BBBP envelope is roughly Rs. 15 lakh to Rs. 40 lakh per year depending on district size and CSR intervention priority. The district magistrate chairs a monthly multi-sector task force with WCD, Health, Education, Police, Anganwadi Services, and the district information officer.

---

## CAG audit findings and independent evaluations

BBBP has drawn credible critical scrutiny that shapes how the programme is being run in 2026. This section is honest about what independent audits have flagged.

The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) 2017 performance audit of BBBP Phase 1 (FY 2015-16 to FY 2016-17) found:

- Only 58% of the Rs. 928 crore Phase 1 allocation was utilised across all states
- 72.6% of utilised funds (Rs. 392.76 crore of Rs. 540.92 crore) went to media and publicity, not direct interventions
- Several states had not constituted district-level task-force committees
- Gender-disaggregated data on outcomes was inconsistent

The Girls First Foundation policy brief (September 2025) revisited the Phase 1 utilisation pattern and confirmed the media-heavy skew, while noting that Phase 2 (FY 2020-21 onwards under Mission Shakti) has shifted the mix towards enforcement and NTL skilling. The 2022 introduction of NTL and the 2025 announcement of the 30% publicity cap are direct responses to the earlier critique.

The factly.in independent analysis and BehanBox reporting on state-level implementation gaps continue to flag that Sikkim, Manipur, and several Northeast states report BBBP data infrequently, making national aggregation harder. WCD Ministry has acknowledged this in Parliamentary responses and initiated a state-level dashboard integration under Mission Shakti Bhavan 2.0.

Reading these critiques alongside the 12-point SRB gain over the decade suggests the honest reading of BBBP in 2026: the awareness push has worked at national aggregate level, but the transition to enforcement plus skilling is still incomplete, and the Haryana 2026 SRB drop is a reminder that gains can reverse without sustained ground-level PC-PNDT enforcement.

---

## State girl-child schemes converged with BBBP

Every state runs one or more girl-child financial-benefit schemes that piggyback on the BBBP awareness ecosystem. Beneficiary families should stack the central SSY plus state scheme plus local Panchayat incentive for maximum benefit.

| State | Scheme | Benefit amount | Eligibility | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Madhya Pradesh | Ladli Lakshmi Yojana | Rs. 1.18 lakh over 21 years in instalments | Girl born after 1 Jan 2006, BPL family | ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in |
| Karnataka | Bhagya Lakshmi Scheme | Rs. 1 lakh maturity value | Girl born to BPL family after 31 Mar 2006 | Karnataka DWCD |
| Uttar Pradesh | Kanya Sumangala Yojana | Rs. 25,000 across 6 education milestones | UP-domiciled girl child | mksy.up.gov.in |
| Bihar | Mukhyamantri Kanya Suraksha Yojana | Rs. 2,000 at birth + Rs. 2,000 at Class 8 | Girl born in Bihar, family income under Rs. 3 lakh | wcdc.bihar.gov.in |
| Haryana | Apni Beti Apna Dhan (revised) | Rs. 25,000 fixed deposit maturing at age 18 | Second girl child in BPL family | wcdhry.gov.in |
| West Bengal | Kanyashree Prakalpa | Rs. 750 to Rs. 25,000 in stages | Unmarried girl aged 13 to 18 in school | wbkanyashree.gov.in |

Stack pattern for a BPL girl child born in Madhya Pradesh in 2026: SSY (open at birth with Rs. 1,000 annual deposit) plus Ladli Lakshmi (Rs. 1.18 lakh across 21 years) plus Panchayat-level birth incentive (Rs. 5,000 in most MP districts). Combined maturity value at girl-child age 21: roughly Rs. 3 lakh plus SSY corpus.

---

## Frequently asked questions

Structured FAQ data with FAQPage JSON-LD is rendered in the FAQ block below the article. A few highlights:

**How do I apply for BBBP?** There is no individual application. BBBP is an awareness and district-intervention scheme. Families access the financial benefit through Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY), which can be opened at any post office or authorised bank in the girl child's name.

**Do I get Rs. 2,100 or a free laptop under BBBP?** No. These are scams. The Ministry of Women and Child Development has issued a public fact-check confirming that websites offering "BBBP jobs, laptop, or mobile for Rs. 2,100" are fake.

**What is the current national Sex Ratio at Birth under BBBP?** 930 girls per 1,000 boys as of FY 2023-24, up from 918 in FY 2014-15, per Ministry of Women and Child Development (PIB PRID 2094929, 21 Jan 2025).

description: Ladli Behna Yojana 2026 MP: Rs 1,500 monthly kist paid, 38th installment on 12 July 2026, Rs 3,000 by 2028 reality check, eligibility and DBT fix guide.
content:
## Ladli Behna Yojana 2026 at a glance

Mukhyamantri Ladli Behna Yojana pays Rs 1,500 a month to about 1.25 crore eligible women across Madhya Pradesh, up from the Rs 1,250 rate that ran until Diwali 2025 when Chief Minister Mohan Yadav sanctioned a Rs 250 hike. The scheme is run by the MP Department of Women and Child Development under portal cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in, and the money hits DBT-enabled Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts on or around the 10th of each month.

The 38th kist was released on 12 July 2026 at a public event in Lahar block of Bhind district. CM Mohan Yadav pressed the transfer button for Rs 1,835 crore to beneficiary accounts (source: Prokerala news wire, 12 July 2026, and APAC News CMO coverage the same day). MP Budget 2026-27 allocates Rs 23,882 crore to Ladli Behna for the full year, per Zee News reporting on the February 2026 budget speech.

One reality check needs stating up front. The Rs 3,000 monthly rate that former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan promised is now targeted for 2028, not 2026 as many WhatsApp forwards claim. The Deccan Herald and Tribune coverage of CM Yadav's recent speeches has been explicit on the 2028 ramp. Anyone budgeting a household around Rs 3,000 arriving in the next six months is planning on the wrong number.

Fresh registration for the scheme has stayed closed since 20 August 2023. There is no general Phase 3 window open in July 2026. Only ad-hoc windows for women who newly cross age 21 or newly marry into MP are being processed. Details on that are in the registration section below.

## Latest kist: what was paid when, and where the CM handed it out

Here's the kist tracker for the 12 months to July 2026, which no finance-site page maintains in a single place.

| Kist no. | Date paid | Amount per woman | Total outlay | CM event location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 27 | 10 Aug 2025 | Rs 1,250 + Rs 250 Raksha Bandhan shagun | Rs 1,875 Cr | Rewa |
| 28 | 10 Sep 2025 | Rs 1,250 | Rs 1,565 Cr | Sagar |
| 29 | 10 Oct 2025 | Rs 1,250 | Rs 1,562 Cr | Ujjain |
| 30 | 10 Nov 2025 | Rs 1,500 (first hiked kist) | Rs 1,834 Cr | Mandsaur |
| 31 | 10 Dec 2025 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,834 Cr | Indore |
| 32 | 10 Jan 2026 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,832 Cr | Jabalpur |
| 33 | 10 Feb 2026 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,830 Cr | Gwalior |
| 34 | 10 Mar 2026 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,832 Cr | Bhopal |
| 35 | 10 Apr 2026 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,833 Cr | Chhindwara |
| 36 | 10 May 2026 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,834 Cr | Rewa |
| 37 | 12 Jun 2026 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,835 Cr | Satna |
| 38 | 12 Jul 2026 | Rs 1,500 | Rs 1,835 Cr | Lahar (Bhind) |

The kist normally lands on the 10th of each month. When the 10th falls on a bank holiday or a Sunday, or when the CM's public event is scheduled a day or two later, credit can slip by 24 to 48 hours. The 12 June and 12 July 2026 pattern reflects event scheduling, not a rule change. The 39th kist is expected around 10 August 2026, and the August month is also when the Rs 250 Raksha Bandhan shagun is paid separately (see one-off payments section).

## Who is eligible

The scheme covers women aged 21 to 60 years who hold Madhya Pradesh domicile and belong to a family whose annual income is Rs 2.5 lakh or less. Unmarried women were formally included from a September 2023 CM announcement, so the earlier "married women only" rule no longer holds. Widowed, divorced, and deserted women were part of the base eligibility from launch in March 2023.

Family landholding must be 5 acres or below. Family means the Samagra family unit as recorded in the MP Samagra ID database, not a nuclear-family definition. The applicant, her husband if married, and dependents linked in Samagra all count for the income and landholding check. Income certificate documentation is not required at application, and the department accepts a self-declaration in the Samagra family record cross-checked against departmental data.

Aadhaar of the applicant must be seeded into a bank account that is DBT-enabled and NPCI-mapped. The Samagra ID must be active for the applicant and her family. e-KYC on the cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in portal must be completed. Any woman whose Samagra ID is inactive, whose Aadhaar is not seeded to a DBT-enabled account, or who has skipped e-KYC will not receive the money regardless of her nominal eligibility.

## Who is not eligible

Anyone from a family where any member is an income tax payer is excluded. This is a family-level test, not an individual test. If your husband, father, or an adult son files an income tax return in any assessment year, the family fails the test even if you personally have zero income.

Anyone from a family where any member is a regular government employee, a permanent government pensioner, a serving member of parliament, or a serving member of the legislative assembly is excluded. Contractual and outsourced workers on state government projects are not treated as regular employees for this test, based on departmental clarifications issued in early 2024.

Families that own a four-wheeler are excluded. A tractor is not counted as a four-wheeler for this rule, given its agricultural use. Commercial goods vehicles registered in a family member's name are treated the same way as private four-wheelers and disqualify the household. Landholding above 5 acres, whether irrigated or unirrigated, also disqualifies the family.

## Rs 3,000 target: what CM Mohan Yadav actually promised and by when

The Rs 3,000 monthly figure originally came from former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan's 2023 assembly election campaign, phrased as a gradual ramp from the launch rate of Rs 1,000. The ramp went Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,250 in October 2023, then held for two years, then to Rs 1,500 from 10 November 2025.

CM Mohan Yadav's public speeches in the first half of 2026 have framed Rs 3,000 as a 2028 target, aligned with the run-up to the next state election cycle. Deccan Herald reported in April 2026 that Yadav told a Mandla event, "Ladli Behna sisters will receive Rs 3,000 by the end of my current tenure." Tribune coverage of the same week added the fiscal reasoning that stepping up to Rs 3,000 in one shot would need close to Rs 47,000 crore a year against the current Rs 23,882 crore MP Budget 2026-27 allocation.

Practical takeaway. Any WhatsApp forward promising Rs 3,000 from the next kist is wrong. The next confirmed hike, if it happens on the current fiscal trajectory, would likely be a step to Rs 2,000 or Rs 2,250 in FY 2026-27 or FY 2027-28, with Rs 3,000 arriving closer to state election year 2028.

## Fresh registration status: why the window is closed and who can still apply

General enrolment closed on 20 August 2023 at the end of Phase 2. Since then, only two narrow windows have opened. A brief window in early 2024 processed newly-turned-21 women whose birthdays fell after the Phase 2 cutoff. A second window in mid-2025 processed newly-married women whose marriages moved them into MP after the Phase 2 cutoff. Both windows were state-notified and closed within weeks.

If you are eligible today and were not enrolled in Phase 1 or Phase 2, watch cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in for a "new registration open" banner and the local Anganwadi centre for physical notice. The department has not committed to a Phase 3 window in 2026, and any coaching centre or aggregator claiming they can enrol you outside the notified window is misleading you.

Women who were enrolled but got dropped in a verification purge, which has been happening on rolling batches since 2024, can raise a grievance through the portal or the helpline. The grievance section below explains the workflow.

## How the money reaches your account

The path is Aadhaar to bank account to DBT to your kist. Every link has to hold or the transfer fails.

Step one is your Aadhaar being seeded into your bank account with NPCI DBT mapping enabled. This is not the same as your Aadhaar being linked to your bank account for KYC purposes. Step two is your Samagra ID being active and correctly linked to your Aadhaar in the MP Samagra database. Step three is e-KYC completion on cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in. Step four is the department's rolling verification confirming your family remains within the income, landholding, and vehicle rules.

When all four hold, the monthly kist is released by the department to your bank on the 10th and reflects the same day or by the next working day. When any one fails, the department flags your record and the kist stops. The two most common failure points are step one (Aadhaar not DBT-mapped) and step three (e-KYC lapse after a document expiry). Both are fixable and covered in the diagnostic section below.

## DBT-linked bank vs Aadhaar-linked bank: the diagnostic flow

DBT-enabled bank account is not the same thing as Aadhaar-linked bank account. This distinction is the single biggest reason women who believe they are eligible do not receive the kist. Bank branch staff sometimes conflate the two, and even literate applicants leave the branch thinking they have done the DBT seeding when they have only done the KYC linking.

Aadhaar-linked bank account means your bank has recorded your Aadhaar number as a KYC document against your account. That is a passive record and does nothing for DBT. DBT-enabled bank account means your bank has submitted an NPCI mapper request to link your Aadhaar as the target for direct benefit transfers. NPCI then maintains the mapping. If NPCI has your Aadhaar mapped to bank A and the department pushes money to bank B where you also hold an account, the money goes to bank A.

Diagnostic flow. First, dial the NPCI Aadhaar Payments Bridge status via any bank's mobile banking app under "check Aadhaar seeding status" or call your bank's customer care and ask specifically for the DBT mapper status. If the mapper is against an old bank account you no longer use, you have found your problem. Second, visit the branch of the bank where you want the kist to arrive and fill an NPCI Aadhaar seeding form. Third, wait 3 to 5 working days for NPCI to update the mapper. Fourth, log into cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in and use the "Aadhaar link and DBT status" option to confirm the department can see the correct mapping. Fifth, expect the next kist to arrive in the new account.

## Documents required

Original enrolment required a small document bundle, since fresh general enrolment is closed the same bundle is still relevant for the narrow newly-turned-21 and newly-married windows plus the grievance and correction workflows.

Aadhaar card of the applicant. Samagra ID of the applicant and her family. Bank passbook or cancelled cheque of the DBT-enabled account. Passport-size photograph. Domicile evidence if not already recorded in Samagra, such as a ration card, voter ID, or MP-issued government document. No income certificate is required because family income is taken from the self-declared Samagra family record.

For newly-married women moving into MP, add a copy of the marriage certificate or an affidavit if the certificate is pending, plus updated Samagra family enrolment showing the applicant's inclusion in the husband's family. For newly-turned-21 women, add a birth certificate or Class 10 marksheet showing the date of birth. Anganwadi workers usually help compile the bundle at the local centre.

## Status check: cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in walkthrough

The portal has a dedicated Application and Payment Status option that works with either the Samagra ID or the Ladli Behna registration number. Open cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in in a browser. Click on "Application and payment status" on the home page. Enter your Samagra family ID or the 12-digit Ladli Behna application number. Enter the captcha shown on screen. Click search.

The result page shows your enrolment status, e-KYC status, DBT mapper status, and a kist-by-kist history with the date and amount of each transfer. If any kist shows "released" but you did not receive the credit in your bank, take a screenshot and raise a grievance from the same portal within seven days. If the e-KYC status shows "pending", complete e-KYC either through the portal's Aadhaar OTP flow or by visiting the local Anganwadi centre.

The portal is available in Hindi and English. Peak evening hours after 8 pm can be slow because of concentrated retail traffic. Morning hours from 7 am to 10 am are usually fastest.

## Ladli Behna cash vs Ladli Behna Awas Yojana: disambiguation

Ladli Behna and Ladli Behna Awas Yojana are two different schemes that share the "Ladli Behna" brand and are constantly confused in WhatsApp forwards. This table settles the difference.

| Feature | Ladli Behna Yojana (cash) | Ladli Behna Awas Yojana (housing) |
|---|---|---|
| Benefit type | Rs 1,500 monthly cash transfer | Rs 2 lakh one-time housing grant |
| Purpose | Monthly income support | Pucca house construction |
| Frequency | Monthly, on the 10th | One-time in instalments during construction |
| Target group | Women 21 to 60, family income Rs 2.5 L or below | Ladli Behna beneficiaries without a pucca house |
| Portal | cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in | cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in with a separate module |
| Enrolment window | Closed for general Phase 3 | Rolling as per state notifications |
| Departmental owner | MP Women and Child Development | MP Rural Development in coordination with WCD |
| Payment mode | DBT to Aadhaar-seeded bank | Instalments to bank tied to construction stages |

If you are eligible for Ladli Behna cash you are also potentially eligible for Ladli Behna Awas provided you do not already have a pucca house registered against your Samagra family. Awas approvals are processed at the block level with Panchayat-level verification of your current housing condition.

## Verification purge risk: what Maharashtra's July 2026 92-lakh removal means for MP beneficiaries

Maharashtra removed 92 lakh names from its Ladki Bahin Yojana beneficiary list in July 2026 after a cross-check with income tax, RTO four-wheeler ownership, and government employment databases. The Times of India and Indian Express coverage on 15 July 2026 pegged the purge at close to Rs 3,000 crore a month in saved outlay for the Maharashtra government.

MP has been running smaller rolling verification purges since 2024, and the departmental circulars in the last quarter have referenced the Maharashtra methodology. A larger purge round in MP over the second half of FY 2026-27 is a live possibility. Beneficiaries who quietly picked up a four-wheeler in the last two years, whose family added an income tax filer, or whose adult son secured a regular government job are the ones most likely to be dropped in the next round.

Practical response. Do a self-audit against the exclusion list in the "who is not eligible" section above. If any exclusion now applies, expect the kist to stop and plan household finances accordingly. Do not treat the monthly Rs 1,500 as guaranteed income. Continuing to receive the money after becoming ineligible carries repayment and legal exposure once the department cross-checks and issues a recovery notice.

## Raksha Bandhan Rs 250 shagun and other one-off payments

The state has paid a Raksha Bandhan shagun of Rs 250 to every Ladli Behna beneficiary along with the August kist for the last three years. It was paid on 10 August 2025 alongside the 27th kist, taking the August 2025 credit to Rs 1,500 per woman (Rs 1,250 base plus Rs 250 shagun). For August 2026, given the current Rs 1,500 base rate, the expected combined credit is Rs 1,750 assuming the same Rs 250 shagun is repeated.

The 2026 Raksha Bandhan festival falls on 9 August. Historical pattern suggests the shagun is credited a day or two before the festival, so 7 to 9 August 2026 is the likely credit window. The regular 39th kist for August 2026 is expected around 10 August. Beneficiaries should check their bank statement for two separate credits, not one lumped credit, given how the department books the two amounts under different budget heads.

Other one-off payments have included a Rs 450 LPG cylinder refill subsidy under the Mukhyamantri Ujjwala scheme for eligible households, credited quarterly, and small Diwali bonuses in some past years. These are separate from the Ladli Behna monthly kist and follow their own eligibility rules.

## Grievance protocol

The Ladli Behna helpline is 0755-2700800. It is answered during MP government working hours, roughly 10 am to 6 pm on weekdays. For questions specific to Aadhaar seeding and DBT mapper, the helpline routes you to your bank's customer care because the mapper sits with NPCI and your bank, not with the department.

Portal-based grievances can be filed on cmladlibahna.mp.gov.in under "Contact us" and "Grievance registration". You need your Samagra ID or Ladli Behna application number and a short description of the issue. A ticket number is generated and the department commits to a 15-day resolution window. In practice, missed-kist tickets tied to DBT mapper issues get resolved faster than eligibility-appeal tickets tied to income or vehicle disputes.

Samagra corrections, for example when your Samagra family record has an incorrect birth date, husband name, or landholding entry, need a separate correction filed at the local Municipal Corporation or Panchayat office responsible for Samagra data. Ladli Behna cannot fix a Samagra data error from its own portal.

## Ambiguous cases: unmarried, transgender, widowed, divorced, deserted

Unmarried women in the 21 to 60 age band are eligible after the September 2023 announcement. The application process for the narrow reopening windows treats them the same as married women, with the household defined by the Samagra family record they belong to (usually their parents' record).

Widowed, divorced, and deserted women have been eligible from launch. Departmental circulars have been explicit that the family income and landholding tests apply to the applicant's current Samagra family record. A widow living independently with her children is assessed on her own family record, not her deceased husband's family of birth.

Transgender women are not explicitly included in the current departmental rules. The portal is silent on gender identity beyond the male / female binary. Applicants who identify as women and hold a transgender identity certificate under the Transgender Persons Act 2019 have reported both approvals and rejections depending on district-level implementation. This is a live ambiguity that has not been formally clarified by the department as of July 2026, and any transgender applicant should get a local NGO or legal aid clinic involved before filing.

content:
## What Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is

Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) is a small-savings account the Union government offers for girl children under the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao campaign. A parent or legal guardian opens the account before the girl turns 10, deposits between Rs. 250 and Rs. 1.5 lakh a year for 15 years, and the corpus earns compound interest until the account matures at 21 years or on the girl's marriage after 18, whichever is earlier.

The current interest rate is 8.2% per year, compounded annually. The Ministry of Finance last confirmed this rate for the July to September 2026 quarter through its quarterly small-savings notification dated 30 June 2026. That's the 8th consecutive quarter the rate has held at 8.2%, unchanged since January 2024.

SSY carries EEE tax status. Deposits qualify for Section 80C (Section 123 under the Income Tax Act 2025) deduction of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh a year, the yearly interest is fully exempt, and the maturity payout is tax-free. Very few investment products in India carry all three exemptions.

---

## Latest interest rate: 8.2% for Q2 FY 2026-27

The Q2 FY 2026-27 rate is 8.2%, effective 1 July to 30 September 2026, per the Ministry of Finance notification of 30 June 2026. This is unchanged from the 8.0% raised on 1 January 2024 to 8.2%, and it's the highest guaranteed rate across all Post Office small-savings schemes for the quarter.

For context, the same quarter's rates for other schemes are: PPF at 7.1%, NSC at 7.7%, and the standard Post Office 5-year Time Deposit at 7.5%. SSY beats every other Central-government guaranteed instrument on both interest and tax status.

Rates are reviewed every quarter by the Ministry of Finance. Any change published in the quarterly notification applies to interest earned from that quarter onwards, not retroactively.

---

## Historical interest rate snapshot

The table captures the SSY rate at the start of each financial year since the scheme launched in December 2014. The rate is a floor for that quarter and may have changed mid-year in some cases; the full quarter-by-quarter series is published on nsiindia.gov.in.

| Financial year | Opening rate | Peak rate that year | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2014-15 | 9.1% | 9.1% | Scheme launched 2 December 2014 |
| 2015-16 | 9.2% | 9.2% | All-time peak rate |
| 2016-17 | 8.6% | 8.6% | First downward revision |
| 2017-18 | 8.4% | 8.4% | Held between 8.3% and 8.4% |
| 2018-19 | 8.1% | 8.5% | Rate rose to 8.5% in Q3 |
| 2019-20 | 8.5% | 8.5% | Peak of the mid-decade cycle |
| 2020-21 | 7.6% | 7.6% | Pandemic-era floor |
| 2021-22 | 7.6% | 7.6% | Held at floor |
| 2022-23 | 7.6% | 7.6% | Held at floor |
| 2023-24 | 8.0% | 8.2% | Raised to 8.2% in January 2024 |
| 2024-25 | 8.2% | 8.2% | Held all four quarters |
| 2025-26 | 8.2% | 8.2% | Held all four quarters |
| 2026-27 | 8.2% | 8.2% (Q1, Q2 confirmed) | 8 consecutive quarters at 8.2% |

The lowest rate in the scheme's history was 7.6% during the pandemic quarters. It has never dipped below that floor.

---

## Who is eligible

You can open an SSY account if your daughter is a resident Indian citizen and below 10 years old on the day of opening. The 10-year cap is strict. If today is her 10th birthday, most branches will refuse the application because she is technically 10 years old, not below 10.

Only a parent or legal guardian can open the account, and only one parent operates it. The account is in the girl's name from day one, but she gains full operating control after she turns 18. Until then, deposits, statements, and withdrawal requests are handled by the guardian.

Each family is allowed a maximum of two SSY accounts, one for each of two daughters. A third account is permitted only in special cases: twins or triplets at the second birth, or twins as the first birth followed by a single girl. The birth certificate has to be submitted as proof.

Non-resident Indian girls are not eligible to open a new account. If a girl becomes NRI after the account is open, the change in residency must be reported and the account is no longer eligible for the standard SSY rate. It typically continues at a lower rate until closure.

---

## Deposit rules and how you can pay

Minimum yearly deposit is Rs. 250 and the maximum is Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year across all accounts of the same girl. Deposits can be made in a single lump or across the year in any number of instalments, and any amount above the minimum is fine as long as the yearly total stays inside the Rs. 250 to Rs. 1.5 lakh band.

Deposits can be made only for the first 15 years from the date of opening. After year 15, the account earns interest for the remaining 6 years without any fresh deposits and matures at year 21. So if you open the account in 2026 for a 1-year-old daughter, your last deposit year is 2041 and the account matures in 2047.

You can deposit through cash at the branch counter, cheque, demand draft, or online through India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) app or the net-banking portal of any authorised bank. Standing instructions for auto-debit are also allowed and are the safest way to avoid missing the yearly minimum.

Interest is calculated on the lowest balance in the account between the 5th and the last day of each calendar month, and credited once, at the end of the financial year on 31 March. Depositing before the 5th of a month gives you a full month of interest on that money.

---

## Worked maturity examples at 8.2%

The four scenarios below use the 8.2% rate held constant across the full 21 years. The numbers come from the government-approved SSY calculator on IndiaPost and match verified figures on Groww and IndianPayCalculator.

**Scenario 1: Rs. 250 per year (bare minimum) for 15 years.** Total deposits Rs. 3,750. Maturity value at year 21: around Rs. 11,970. Tax-free gain: Rs. 8,220. This shows even a minimum-effort account roughly triples the money over 21 years thanks to compounding.

**Scenario 2: Rs. 1,000 per month (Rs. 12,000 per year) for 15 years.** Total deposits Rs. 1,80,000. Maturity value at year 21: Rs. 5,74,570. Tax-free gain: Rs. 3,94,570. This is a realistic middle-income scenario, and the interest earned is more than double the principal.

**Scenario 3: Rs. 5,000 per month (Rs. 60,000 per year) for 15 years.** Total deposits Rs. 9,00,000. Maturity value at year 21: around Rs. 26.5 lakh. Tax-free gain: Rs. 17.5 lakh. Suitable for salaried families using SSY as part of the tax-saving basket.

**Scenario 4: Rs. 1.5 lakh per year (maximum) for 15 years.** Total deposits Rs. 22,50,000. Maturity value at year 21: Rs. 71,82,119. Tax-free gain: Rs. 49,32,119. The interest alone is more than twice the total invested, and every rupee is exempt from tax.

Interest rate revisions during the 21-year window will move these numbers. Every 0.1% change in the average rate over 21 years shifts the Scenario 4 maturity by roughly Rs. 1 lakh. That's why the current 8-quarter streak at 8.2% is treated as a favourable window by tax-planners.

---

## Tax benefits under old vs new tax regime

SSY's tax status depends on which income-tax regime you file under, and this is the single most-missed point in most SSY guides.

Under the old tax regime, SSY is a true EEE instrument. Deposits up to Rs. 1.5 lakh a year qualify for a deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act 1961, or the equivalent Section 123 of the Income Tax Act 2025. Interest earned each year is fully exempt. The maturity amount and any partial withdrawal are also tax-free.

Under the new tax regime (default from FY 2023-24), the upfront Section 80C deduction does not apply. You lose the tax saving on the Rs. 1.5 lakh deposit, but the interest and maturity payouts remain tax-free. So SSY becomes an EE (Exempt-Exempt) product for new-regime filers rather than EEE.

The practical decision: if you're on the old tax regime and using the full Rs. 1.5 lakh 80C bucket, SSY is one of the top three uses of that bucket alongside PPF and ELSS. If you're on the new tax regime, SSY is still worth it for the tax-free 8.2% compounding, but the deposit itself gives no upfront tax relief. Compare against PPF (same tax treatment, 7.1% rate) and direct equity mutual funds (higher expected return but taxable at 12.5% LTCG above Rs. 1.25 lakh).

---

## Maturity, partial withdrawal, and premature closure

The account matures 21 years from opening. Whichever of these two events comes first triggers the payout: reaching year 21, or the girl marrying at any age above 18. On maturity, the full corpus (principal plus interest) is credited to the girl's own bank account.

Partial withdrawal is allowed once the girl turns 18 or completes Class 10, whichever is earlier. Up to 50% of the balance at the end of the previous financial year can be withdrawn, and the money must be used for higher education or school fees. Withdrawal can be a single lump or up to five yearly instalments over the following years.

Premature closure is allowed in three narrow cases: girl's marriage after 18 (window is one month before to three months after the marriage date), death of the account holder (payout to the nominee at the standard SSY rate), or a case of extreme compassion certified by the district authority (medical emergency, terminal illness, or death of the guardian). Compassionate closure pays interest at the Post Office savings account rate for the period after year 5, not the SSY rate.

Closure on change of residency to NRI is mandatory. The account can no longer continue at the SSY rate once the girl's status changes.

---

## How to open an SSY account

You can open the account at any India Post branch or at any of the 11 authorised banks: State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Union Bank of India, IDBI Bank, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Bank of India.

Documents required: the girl's birth certificate (mandatory, no substitute), a photo ID and address proof of the guardian (Aadhaar, PAN, passport, or voter ID), passport-size photos of the guardian and the girl, and a filled Form 1 (Account Opening) which is available at the branch or downloadable from nsiindia.gov.in.

Take the documents and the first deposit (minimum Rs. 250) to the branch. The branch verifies documents, opens the account, and hands over a passbook. Some banks now offer a digital opening flow for existing customers where documents are pulled via the KYC record and only the first deposit needs to be made at the branch.

Once opened, all further deposits and status checks can be done online through IPPB app (for post office accounts) or through the bank's net-banking portal (for bank-held accounts).

---

## SSY compared to PPF, NSC, and ELSS

Every parent shopping for tax-advantaged savings looks at these four together. The table below shows how they compare on the metrics that matter for a long-term goal like a daughter's education or marriage.

| Metric | SSY | PPF | NSC | ELSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current rate (Q2 FY 2026-27) | 8.2% | 7.1% | 7.7% | Market-linked (12-15% typical) |
| Lock-in | 21 years (deposits 15) | 15 years extendable | 5 years | 3 years |
| Minimum deposit | Rs. 250 per year | Rs. 500 per year | Rs. 100 per certificate | Rs. 500 per SIP |
| Maximum deposit for 80C | Rs. 1.5 lakh | Rs. 1.5 lakh | No cap on principal (80C capped at Rs. 1.5 lakh) | Rs. 1.5 lakh |
| Tax on interest | Exempt | Exempt | Taxable (though 80C-deductible if reinvested) | Exempt below Rs. 1.25 lakh LTCG a year, else 12.5% |
| Tax on maturity | Exempt | Exempt | Interest at maturity is taxable | 12.5% LTCG above Rs. 1.25 lakh |
| Who can invest | Guardian for girl below 10 | Any resident individual | Any resident individual | Any resident |

SSY wins on rate and tax status for the specific use case it was built for: long-horizon savings for a girl. PPF is the best gender-neutral EEE option. NSC works for shorter 5-year lock-ins. ELSS has the shortest lock-in and highest expected return but comes with market risk and partial tax on gains.

---

## Transfer, dormant revival, and nomination

The account can be transferred between two branches of the same institution (post office to post office, or bank to bank) or between institutions (post office to bank, or vice versa). Transfer is free if the reason is a change of the guardian's residence with proof; otherwise a Rs. 100 fee applies. The receiving branch takes over all further transactions once the transfer paperwork completes, typically in 15 to 30 days.

If you miss the Rs. 250 minimum in any year, the account turns dormant. To revive it, pay the outstanding minimum for each defaulted year plus a Rs. 50 penalty per defaulted year and deposit at least Rs. 250 for the current year. Revival is allowed any time within the 15-year deposit window, so a dormant account can be resurrected without permanent damage.

Nomination is allowed at the time of opening or later. The nominee receives the maturity amount if the account holder passes away before maturity. Nomination can be changed by submitting Form 2 (Nomination) at the branch. Most branches recommend adding the guardian as nominee at opening to keep the process smooth if anything happens later.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the current SSY interest rate?** SSY earns 8.2% per year for the July to September 2026 quarter, per the Ministry of Finance notification of 30 June 2026. This is the 8th consecutive quarter at 8.2%.

**Up to what age can I open an SSY account for my daughter?** SSY requires the girl to be below 10 years old on the date of opening. Once opened, the account runs for 21 years, so opening it at birth gives the longest compounding runway.

**Is SSY tax-free under both old and new tax regimes?** Interest and maturity are tax-free under both regimes. The Section 80C or Section 123 deduction on the yearly deposit is available only under the old tax regime.

**Can I open SSY for my son?** No. SSY is exclusively for girl children. Sons can be covered under general instruments like PPF or ELSS instead.

**What if I skip a year's minimum deposit?** The account turns dormant. Revive it any time within 15 years by paying the missed minimums plus a Rs. 50 penalty per missed year and the current year's Rs. 250.

**Can husband and wife both claim the 80C deduction on the same SSY account?** No. Only the parent who actually made the deposit and whose PAN is linked to the account can claim it. Splitting the yearly deposit across both parents' PANs is not permitted for the same account.

**How much can I withdraw before maturity?** Up to 50% of the balance at the end of the previous financial year, and only after the girl turns 18 or completes Class 10. The withdrawal has to be used for higher education or school fees.

**What happens if the SSY interest rate changes during the 21-year period?** Interest is credited at whatever rate the Ministry of Finance announces for that quarter. Historical rates ranged from 7.6% (pandemic floor) to 9.2% (2015-16 peak). The rate in your opening year does not lock in for the full 21 years.

**Can I open SSY in a bank rather than the post office?** Yes. The 11 authorised banks (SBI, PNB, BoB, Canara, Union, IDBI, ICICI, HDFC, Axis, Kotak, BoI) offer SSY at the same terms and same interest rate as the post office.

**What documents do I need to open the account?** Girl's birth certificate, guardian's photo ID and address proof, passport-size photos, and Form 1. The birth certificate is mandatory and has no substitute; hospital discharge summary or Aadhaar are not accepted.

All 11 accept walk-in openings; SBI, HDFC, and ICICI also offer partial digital flows for existing KYC-verified customers.

content:
## MKSY 2026 at a glance

Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana (MKSY) is the Uttar Pradesh government's 6-tranche direct benefit transfer scheme that now pays a total of Rs 25,000 to every eligible girl child from birth through graduation, up from the earlier Rs 15,000 ceiling. The Department of Women Welfare runs the scheme through mksy.up.gov.in, and the Directorate of Women Welfare at Lucknow is the nodal implementing agency. Payments land directly in the mother's Aadhaar-seeded bank account, or the guardian's account where the mother is absent.

The 2026-27 revision is the headline change most competitor pages have not yet caught. The old scheme paid Rs 15,000 in six instalments. The revised structure keeps the six life-stage triggers but raises the total payout to Rs 25,000. Around 26.81 lakh girls have received benefits under MKSY up to early 2026, and cumulative registrations since the scheme launched on 25 April 2019 have crossed 1.5 crore, per the Directorate of Women Welfare (mahilakalyan.up.nic.in). The state has earmarked roughly Rs 400 crore for MKSY in the FY 2026-27 budget line for the Women and Child Development demand for grants, per the UP Budget 2026-27 speech as analysed by Drishti IAS.

The programme sits inside the state's broader package for the girl child, alongside Beti Bachao Beti Padhao awareness activities and central schemes like Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. MKSY is the only UP-run scheme that pays cash directly at every major milestone from birth to Class 12 pass and degree admission, so it is the single most important application a UP family should file for a daughter born after 1 April 2019.

## The 6 tranches: what you get and when

The revised MKSY structure keeps six categories aligned to life-stage milestones. The tranche split below is per the official MKSY presentation on mksy.up.gov.in and the Directorate of Women Welfare communications, and it totals Rs 25,000 after the 2026-27 hike.

| Category | Life-stage trigger | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Birth of the girl child (after 1 April 2019) | Rs 5,000 |
| 2 | Completion of full vaccination up to 1 year of age | Rs 2,000 |
| 3 | Admission in Class 1 in a recognised school | Rs 3,000 |
| 4 | Admission in Class 6 in a recognised school | Rs 3,000 |
| 5 | Admission in Class 9 in a recognised school | Rs 5,000 |
| 6 | Class 12 pass and admission to degree or diploma course of at least 2 years | Rs 7,000 |
| Total |  | Rs 25,000 |

Category 1 is filed by the mother or guardian soon after the girl's birth, using the birth certificate as proof. Category 2 needs the immunisation card showing all vaccines completed as per the UP government schedule up to age 1. Category 3, 4, and 5 need the school admission proof for the relevant class. Category 6 needs the Class 12 marksheet plus the degree or diploma admission letter.

The old Rs 15,000 total was widely quoted on state-scheme aggregator sites and it is the number many families still assume applies. The revised Rs 25,000 total applies to fresh applications and to ongoing beneficiaries whose next tranche falls due after the revision date. Check the current disbursal schedule on mksy.up.gov.in under the beneficiary login before assuming any specific amount for your case.

## Who is eligible

Any girl child born on or after 1 April 2019 to a family that is a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh is eligible, subject to the household income and family-composition rules below. There is no caste-based restriction and no distinction between rural and urban applicants.

Domicile: the family must hold a UP domicile certificate or valid proof of continuous residence in the state. Employees of the state government posted temporarily outside UP are considered domiciled. Migrant families who have moved to UP recently must produce a domicile certificate before the first tranche can be released.

Income ceiling: annual family income must not exceed Rs 3 lakh from all sources combined, and this ceiling has not changed under the 2026-27 revision. A valid income certificate from the local tehsil office is mandatory at the time of application. Families slightly above the ceiling are not covered, and MKSY does not have a partial-benefit tier.

Family cap: a maximum of two girls per family can be enrolled under MKSY. The important exception is that if the second birth results in twins or the first birth results in triplets, all three girls are covered, so up to 3 girls from a single family are permitted in twin or triplet scenarios. Adopted orphan girls also count within the two-girl family cap.

Bank account: the beneficiary parent, usually the mother, must have a single-holder savings bank account with Aadhaar seeded through the NPCI Mapper. DBT transfers land only in Aadhaar-seeded accounts, so a fresh bank account without seeding cannot receive tranche payments.

## Edge cases: orphan, adopted, twin, triplet, guardianship, joint account

Real families rarely match the plain-vanilla eligibility case. The table below covers the most common edge cases handled by the Directorate of Women Welfare through district-level clarifications.

| Case | Treatment under MKSY | What to file |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan girl in a care home | Eligible via legal guardian or Child Welfare Committee (CWC) | CWC guardianship order plus care home certificate |
| Adopted girl child | Eligible, counts within the 2-girl family cap of the adoptive family | Adoption deed plus revised birth certificate |
| Twin daughters (second birth) | Both eligible, family cap extended from 2 to 3 for that family | Twin birth certificate from hospital or municipal record |
| Triplet daughters (first birth) | All three eligible, family cap extended to 3 | Triplet birth certificate |
| Child under guardianship (parents deceased) | Eligible, guardian's account used for DBT | Guardianship order from competent court or CWC |
| Joint account with father | Rejected at NPCI Mapper stage | Open single-holder account in mother's name, seed Aadhaar |
| Divorced or separated mother | Eligible, mother's account used | Custody order or affidavit plus mother's individual account |
| Girl already receiving another state cash scheme | Still eligible for MKSY, no clash rule | Standard MKSY documents |

The joint-account case is the single most common preventable rejection. Bank branches often open joint accounts by default when a mother visits for a new savings account with a minor daughter. DBT under MKSY needs the mother's individual account with her own Aadhaar seeded through the NPCI Mapper. If the account is joint with the father or another adult, the Mapper flags a conflict and the tranche transaction fails.

## How to apply on mksy.up.gov.in

The online application on mksy.up.gov.in is the primary channel. Offline application through the local Anganwadi centre or the Block Development Officer's office is available where internet access is limited, but the offline form still gets keyed into the same portal, so most families are better off filing directly online.

Step 1: open mksy.up.gov.in and click Citizen Services, then Apply Online. Read the guidelines and tick the declaration. Enter the applicant mother's name, mobile number, and email if any.

Step 2: verify the mobile number with the OTP sent by the portal. Set a login password. The portal creates a user account under your mobile number.

Step 3: log in and select New Application, then choose the tranche category for which you are filing. Category 1 for a newborn, Category 2 for a girl who has completed full vaccination at 1 year, and so on. Each tranche needs its own application even if the same girl is the beneficiary.

Step 4: enter the girl child's details, family details, income certificate number, domicile certificate number, and bank account details of the mother. The Aadhaar number of the mother is mandatory.

Step 5: upload scanned copies of the documents required for the specific tranche. File size limits are printed on each upload field. Portrait-mode photos are usually rejected for poor legibility, so use a scanner app that outputs A4 landscape PDFs.

Step 6: submit and note the registration ID displayed on screen. Also check the SMS sent to the registered mobile for the same ID. This ID is the tracking key for every future status check.

Step 7: the application first goes to the local Anganwadi worker for beneficiary verification, then to the Block Development Officer, then to the District Probation Officer, and finally to the Directorate for DBT release. Standard timeline is 30 to 60 days for a clean application.

## Documents required per tranche

Every tranche needs a different combination because the trigger event changes at each life stage. The common documents across all tranches are the mother's Aadhaar, mother's bank passbook first page or cancelled cheque, UP domicile certificate, income certificate, family ID or ration card, and the mother's passport photograph. The tranche-specific documents are listed below.

Category 1 (birth): the girl's birth certificate issued by the municipal or panchayat authority. Hospital birth records alone are not accepted, the civil registration certificate is what the portal recognises.

Category 2 (vaccination): the immunisation card signed by the ANM or Medical Officer, showing all vaccines completed as per the UP government schedule up to age 1. Card must be legible and stamped.

Category 3 (Class 1 admission): the school admission letter or bonafide certificate on school letterhead, plus the fee receipt for the current academic session. Private and government schools are both accepted provided the school is recognised by the state.

Category 4 (Class 6 admission): same as Category 3 but for Class 6. Continuity of schooling is not a strict rule, so a girl who moved schools between Class 5 and Class 6 is still eligible.

Category 5 (Class 9 admission): same as Category 3 but for Class 9.

Category 6 (Class 12 pass plus degree or diploma admission): the Class 12 marksheet from a recognised board (UP Board, CBSE, ICSE, or other Class 12 equivalent), plus the admission letter for a degree or diploma course of at least 2 years duration. Vocational and skill diplomas of at least 2 years are accepted.

Documents that families forget most often are the income certificate (assumed valid but issued years ago and now expired), the current-session school fee receipt (only the admission letter is uploaded), and the mother's cancelled cheque (uploaded from an old account that is no longer active). Refresh these before you start the application.

## The Category 2 vaccination trap

Many families file Category 1 at birth, receive the Rs 5,000 credit, and then assume the next Rs 2,000 vaccination tranche will trigger automatically once the immunisation card is complete at age 1. It does not. Category 2 needs a fresh, separate application on mksy.up.gov.in with the immunisation card upload, filed by the same mother's login.

The gap between Category 1 disbursal at about 30 to 60 days after birth and the Category 2 filing window at the girl's first birthday is roughly 10 to 11 months. Most families forget the follow-up. The Directorate publishes reminders through Anganwadi workers but tracking coverage is uneven at the village level.

Two practical checks. First, save the mksy.up.gov.in login credentials and the registration ID in a family document so the reminder is visible when the girl turns one. Second, ask the Anganwadi worker at the annual immunisation visit whether she can help file the Category 2 application on the spot. Many Anganwadi centres have a portal login and can key in the application for you if you carry the required documents.

The same reminder logic applies at Class 1, Class 6, Class 9, and Class 12 admission. Each tranche needs a fresh application filed within the same mother's mksy.up.gov.in account. Missing a tranche is not a permanent loss, and back-dated filing within the same academic session is usually accepted, but delays beyond one session are rejected.

## Top 5 rejection reasons with fixes

Rejection data below is aggregated from district probation office grievance registers and beneficiary support helpline call summaries through Q1 FY 2026-27, published as part of the Directorate's quarterly review.

| Rejection reason | Why it happens | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Name or DOB mismatch across documents | Aadhaar, birth certificate, and school records show different spellings or dates | Correct all documents to match Aadhaar spelling and DOB before filing, use the CSC centre for Aadhaar update |
| NPCI Mapper conflict on bank account | Mother's Aadhaar seeded on multiple bank accounts, or seeded on a joint account | Deactivate old accounts, re-seed Aadhaar on one single-holder account only, confirm via bank branch |
| Income certificate expired | Certificate older than 6 months or issued for a previous financial year | Get a fresh income certificate from the tehsil office before filing, valid for the current FY |
| Birth certificate DOB mismatch | Municipal birth certificate shows a different date from Aadhaar | Reconcile at the municipal office first, then update Aadhaar to match, or vice versa depending on which is correct |
| Duplicate application for same girl | Two applications filed by different family members for the same tranche | Withdraw one at the DPO office, keep only the mother's application active |

Fixing an NPCI Mapper conflict often takes 2 to 3 branch visits because the bank staff need to first de-seed Aadhaar from the older account, confirm de-seeding at the NPCI Mapper, and then re-seed on the new account. Allow at least 15 working days for the mapper database to refresh before re-filing the tranche application.

## Aadhaar-DBT bank seeding: why the mother's individual account matters

DBT under MKSY is routed through the NPCI Aadhaar Payment Bridge (APB). The Aadhaar number acts as the destination address, and the NPCI Mapper stores exactly one active bank account against each Aadhaar. If the mother's Aadhaar is seeded on account A but the MKSY application quotes account B, the tranche transaction fails at APB with a mapper mismatch, and the amount is refunded to the state treasury.

Two conditions must hold. First, the mother's Aadhaar must be seeded on exactly one bank account, and that account must be a single-holder savings account in her name. Second, the account details entered in the MKSY application must exactly match that Aadhaar-seeded account, including the IFSC code and the account number.

To check the current seeding status, visit uidai.gov.in, log in with the Aadhaar number, and check the Bank Seeding Status page. Alternatively, dial *99*99*1# from the mobile number registered with Aadhaar and follow the prompts. If seeding is on the wrong account, visit the correct bank branch with the Aadhaar and passbook, request de-seeding from the old account, and re-seed on the new one. Most banks now handle this at the branch counter in under 30 minutes.

Joint accounts with a parent, spouse, or other relative are not compatible with DBT. Even if the mother is the primary holder, the presence of a joint holder causes NPCI Mapper conflicts in a majority of cases. If your existing account is joint, either open a new single-holder account in the mother's name and re-seed, or convert the joint account to single-holder at the branch (which requires the second holder's consent and a fresh KYC).

## Status check: aadhaar, registration ID, mobile

Applicants can track a MKSY application through three tracks on mksy.up.gov.in.

Track by registration ID: open the Track Application section on mksy.up.gov.in, enter the registration ID printed on the acknowledgment slip, and view the current stage. Stages progress from Submitted, to Anganwadi Verified, to Block Approved, to District Approved, to DBT Released.

Track by mother's mobile number: log in with the mobile number and password set at registration, and view all applications filed under that mobile. Each tranche appears as a separate row.

Track by DBT transaction: for a tranche that shows DBT Released but no credit in the bank account, check the PFMS portal at pfms.nic.in under Know Your Payments, entering the mother's bank account and IFSC. The PFMS confirmation is authoritative for whether the state actually released the money.

If PFMS shows a release but the bank passbook does not, the issue is at the bank end, usually an NPCI Mapper conflict or dormant account. Take the PFMS reference number to the bank branch for reconciliation.

## Grievance escalation ladder

The Directorate publishes a defined escalation ladder for beneficiaries who cannot get their application moved or their tranche credited. Use each step in order. Skipping levels usually results in the complaint being routed back down the ladder, which wastes time.

Step 1: raise a grievance through the mksy.up.gov.in portal under Beneficiary Login, then Support, then New Ticket. Include the registration ID and describe the exact issue in plain terms.

Step 2: contact the District Probation Officer (DPO) of your district if the portal ticket is not resolved in 15 working days. DPO contact details are listed on mahilakalyan.up.nic.in under District Officers.

Step 3: escalate to the Directorate of Women Welfare, Lucknow, through the email mksy-up@gov.in with the registration ID, DPO reference number, and copies of the earlier tickets.

Step 4: call the state helpline 1800-180-1111. This is the general UP government helpline that logs the complaint and routes it to the Directorate for a written response.

Step 5: if the issue involves fund flow rather than application processing, file a PFMS grievance through pfms.nic.in with the DBT reference number.

Most application-level issues get resolved by step 2 or step 3. Bank-side issues need step 5 because the state's role ends at the DBT release event.

## UNICEF 2026 evaluation: what the report found

The UNICEF India office, working with the UP government, published an evaluation study titled MKSY Model for Empowerment in March 2026 (available on unicef.org/india/reports). The report reviewed the scheme's design, implementation, and beneficiary outcomes across 15 UP districts covering high-enrolment as well as underserved regions.

Key findings from the study, useful for anyone assessing the scheme's real impact. Registration coverage of eligible girls has improved from about 55 percent in 2021 to over 70 percent by end of 2025 in the surveyed districts, per the UNICEF study. The Rs 5,000 birth tranche has measurable positive effects on institutional delivery rates and early childhood nutrition access, based on comparison with matched control households. School admission tranches at Class 1, 6, and 9 correlate with reduced dropout rates in the covered cohort, though the report notes causality is difficult to isolate because of parallel schemes.

The study also flagged three implementation gaps that the state committed to address. Category 2 vaccination tranche uptake is lower than expected because families forget the follow-up filing at age 1. Rural NPCI Mapper conflicts remain a top rejection driver. And digital literacy at the beneficiary end limits self-service on mksy.up.gov.in, making Anganwadi assistance important for large parts of rural UP.

The UNICEF citation is worth including in any documentation family shares with school administrators or bank branches to establish the scheme's legitimacy. Some private schools still ask for supporting government letters before recognising the admission tranche as valid non-fee income.

## Common confusion

Private school eligibility: MKSY does not distinguish between government, aided, and private schools for the Class 1, 6, 9, and 12 admission tranches. The only test is whether the school is recognised by the state education board or a national board like CBSE or ICSE. Fee-paying private schools are eligible.

Hostel-linked benefits: MKSY tranches are direct cash transfers to the mother's account. There is no separate hostel component. If the girl lives in a hostel, the tranche is still credited to the mother's account and the family manages the fund internally.

One-time vs multi-tranche: MKSY is not a one-time grant. It is a life-stage-triggered series of six separate cash transfers. Each tranche needs a fresh application on mksy.up.gov.in with the trigger-event proof.

Overlap with Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY): SSY is a central small savings scheme for the girl child that grows through parental deposits. MKSY is state cash directly credited at milestones. Both can be operated in parallel for the same girl. There is no rule barring dual enrolment.

Overlap with UP scholarship schemes: girls who receive UP scholarship at Class 9 or Class 12 continue to be eligible for the MKSY tranche at the same class. There is no clawback.

## Primary sources

- MKSY official portal: https://mksy.up.gov.in
- Directorate of Women Welfare, UP: https://mahilakalyan.up.nic.in
- MKSY Presentation PDF: https://mksy.up.gov.in/women_welfare/pdf/MKSY-Presentation.pdf
- UNICEF India MKSY Model for Empowerment (March 2026): https://www.unicef.org/india/reports
- UP Budget 2026-27 analysis (Drishti IAS): https://www.drishtiias.com
- PFMS DBT tracking: https://pfms.nic.in
- NPCI Aadhaar Payment Bridge status: https://uidai.gov.in

The scheme's biggest single lever is a mother's single-holder Aadhaar-seeded bank account and a saved mksy.up.gov.in login for the reminder chain from Category 1 through Category 6.

faqs.answer: No. MKSY tranches are paid through the NPCI Aadhaar Payment Bridge, so the mother's Aadhaar must be seeded on exactly one single-holder savings bank account. Applications from families with unseeded Aadhaar are approved but the DBT transaction fails at the payment stage and the amount is refunded to the state treasury. Seed Aadhaar on the correct account before filing, and confirm the seeding status through uidai.gov.in or by dialling *99*99*1# from the registered mobile.
faqs.question: Can I apply for MKSY without linking Aadhaar to a bank account?

faqs.answer: The default MKSY family cap is two girls per family, but this cap extends to three in twin or triplet cases. If the second birth results in twin daughters, both are eligible along with any earlier daughter, giving the family up to 3 covered girls. If the first birth results in triplet daughters, all three are eligible. Attach the twin or triplet birth certificate from the hospital or municipal record with each Category 1 application, and file a separate application for each girl using the same mother's mksy.up.gov.in login.
faqs.question: How do twins or triplets apply for Kanya Sumangala Yojana?

faqs.answer: The family income limit for MKSY 2026 is Rs 3 lakh per year from all sources combined, and this ceiling has not changed under the 2026-27 revision. A valid income certificate issued by the local tehsil office within the current financial year is required at the time of every tranche application. Families with income slightly above Rs 3 lakh are not covered, and MKSY does not have a partial-benefit tier for higher-income households. UP domicile is a separate mandatory requirement in addition to the income ceiling.
faqs.question: What is the income limit for MKSY 2026?
