description: Bihar Ration Card 2026 apply guide: 6.85 cr holders, 1.65 cr e-KYC pending, epds.bihar.gov.in steps, PHH AAY types and June-August clubbed distribution.
content:
## Bihar ration card 2026 at a glance

Bihar has 6.85 crore ration card holders on the rolls of the Department of Food, Consumer Protection and Public Distribution, which makes it the second largest state PDS in India after Uttar Pradesh. Every operation on the card, from new application to status check to e-ration card download, runs through the state portal at epds.bihar.gov.in.

Two live 2026 numbers matter more than any other before you file a fresh application. The department set 31 March 2026 as the hard deadline for Aadhaar e-KYC of every household member above age 5, and 5.2 crore holders completed the e-KYC by the deadline, per department reporting cited by regional dailies. The remaining 1.65 crore holders are still pending, and the department has flagged suspension risk for households that do not complete e-KYC at their Fair Price Shop (FPS) in the coming distribution cycles.

The second live number is the clubbed distribution decision. The department announced that the June, July, and August 2026 monthly quotas will be released together in a single distribution window at every FPS across the state. The reason is flood-season supply logistics. Bihar's monsoon typically stresses road access to riverine districts (Muzaffarpur, Sitamarhi, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Saharsa, Katihar, Kishanganj, Araria, Purnia, Supaul), and a single consolidated release lets the department pre-position stock at the FPS before the roads become unreliable.

If you land here to apply for a new card, complete pending e-KYC, download your e-ration card, or add a family member, every route is covered below with the exact epds.bihar.gov.in step, the document stack, and the escalation ladder if the file is stuck.

The Bihar page draws its authority from the department, from the national NFSA framework administered by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and from primary reporting on the e-KYC drive and clubbed distribution announcement. Every dated stat below is attributed inline in the sentence it appears in.

## Who is eligible for a Bihar ration card in 2026

Any resident household of Bihar within the state's Priority Household inclusion criteria is eligible under the National Food Security Act 2013 (NFSA). Bihar does not publish a hard rupee ceiling for state-wide Priority Household (PHH) eligibility. The department uses NFSA priority scoring instead, based on housing type, primary occupation of the head of family, and social-deprivation criteria.

The priority-scoring model draws from the Socio Economic Caste Census 2011 (SECC) data as updated by the department during the 2015-16 rollout, and revised through periodic district-level surveys. Households classified as priority under the SECC and subsequent surveys, or households that meet the state-notified inclusion criteria (kutcha house, no adult earning member, scheduled tribe household in scheduled areas, transgender person as head of family, single-woman household, senior citizen with no support), rank first in the state's PHH allocation.

Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY), the poorest-of-poor slab, has criteria-based eligibility rather than income-only. In Bihar the AAY criteria are widow with no earning male member, disabled with 40 percent or higher disability and no earning member, elderly above 60 with no adult earning support, tribal households in scheduled areas, and destitute households identified by the gram panchayat or urban local body. AAY households get 35 kg of grain per household per month.

The exclusion criteria that disqualify a household from any NFSA slab in Bihar are three, and they apply state-wide. A household with an income tax filer among adult members. A household owning a four-wheeler passenger vehicle registered in an adult member's name. A household where an adult member is a government employee at the state or central level. These exclusions are checked at the district office during application verification.

Nationality is Indian citizen. Every listed member above age 5 must complete Aadhaar e-KYC, which is now mandatory statewide and drove the March 2026 deadline discussed in the next section.

## Types of ration cards offered by Bihar

Bihar issues three ration card categories on its EPDS system, and each carries a different grain quantum and price.

Priority Household (PHH) is the main NFSA slab in Bihar and covers the bulk of the 6.85 crore holders on the state rolls. PHH households get 5 kg of grain per person per month at zero cost under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), which was extended by the Union Cabinet on 29 November 2023 through 31 December 2028. Before PMGKAY, PHH households paid Rs 3 per kg for rice and Rs 2 per kg for wheat under the NFSA issue price, but the current free distribution supersedes that pricing.

Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) is the poorest-of-poor slab. AAY households in Bihar get 35 kg of grain per household per month at zero cost under PMGKAY, regardless of the family size. AAY cards in Bihar are colour-marked and receive priority handling at the FPS during distribution.

Anna Yojana pink card is Bihar's state-level overlay on top of the central NFSA classification. The pink card was rolled out by the state government to extend PDS coverage to households that ranked just below the NFSA cutoff on the state priority-scoring model but were considered vulnerable by the district administration. Pink card households draw a state-notified quantum funded partly by the state exchequer and partly through the NFSA channel. The pink overlay is not universal across all districts and is issued on a demand-based rolling model through the block office.

Non-Priority Household (NPHH), the fourth category recognised nationally, exists on the Bihar EPDS database as a record of households outside NFSA eligibility, but does not draw subsidised NFSA grain. NPHH is not actively marketed by the department because the state-level Anna Yojana pink overlay covers the near-miss households that would otherwise sit in NPHH.

Pick the category that matches your household situation, not the highest-quantum one. AAY criteria are strict and applying under AAY without meeting the widow, disability, elderly, or tribal criteria delays the file.

## The 1.65 crore e-KYC pending crisis, and what to do if you missed the 31 March 2026 deadline

The department set 31 March 2026 as the hard deadline for Aadhaar e-KYC of every listed member above age 5 on every ration card in Bihar. As of the latest reporting, 5.2 crore holders completed e-KYC by the deadline, but 1.65 crore holders are still pending, per regional dailies covering the department's May 2026 review.

Pending households face suspension risk. Once the department flags a card for non-compliance, the ePoS device at the FPS blocks the monthly draw until e-KYC is completed for every listed member. This means a household that was drawing 25 kg of grain per month (5 members at 5 kg each) can be reduced to zero if none of the listed members complete e-KYC in the current cycle.

If you missed the 31 March 2026 deadline, the good news is that late e-KYC is still accepted at your FPS free of cost. Here is the exact sequence to complete late e-KYC and restore your household's active status.

1. Confirm which members are pending. Visit epds.bihar.gov.in, log in with your ration card number and Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP, and open the household member list. Members with a red "KYC Pending" tag are the ones you need to bring to the FPS.

2. Take every pending member to the FPS during working hours (typically 8 AM to 12 noon and 4 PM to 8 PM). Bring the original Aadhaar card of each pending member. The FPS dealer runs Aadhaar-based e-KYC on the ePoS device using fingerprint biometric first, falling back to iris scan or OTP if fingerprint fails.

3. Vulnerable members (elderly with worn fingerprints, disabled members, small children between age 5 and age 10) should attempt iris scan or OTP on the ePoS. All ePoS devices deployed by the department support all three authentication modes.

4. Ask the FPS dealer to print the e-KYC acknowledgment slip for each member. Keep the slip until the next month's distribution to confirm reactivation.

5. Household reactivation reflects on the state portal within 48 to 72 hours. If the card still shows "Suspended" after 7 days, escalate to the Block Supply Officer (BSO) at the block office with the acknowledgment slips.

6. If the FPS dealer refuses to run e-KYC or claims the ePoS is out of order for more than 3 days in a row, file a grievance on the Bihar Public Grievance Redressal System (BPGRS) portal or call the department toll-free number 1800-345-6194.

Do not pay any middleman or cyber cafe for e-KYC. The service is free at every FPS across Bihar, and any charge is an unauthorised extraction.

## Documents required for a new Bihar ration card

The document stack for a new Bihar ration card is deliberately kept short by the department, and self-declaration is accepted for the income part.

Identity and address proofs form the base layer. Aadhaar card of every household member (mandatory e-KYC above age 5). One address proof from voter ID, electricity bill, rent agreement, or municipal water bill of the head of family. Passport-size family group photograph covering all listed members.

Income and eligibility proofs form the second layer. Self-declaration of household income on the state-prescribed format (Bihar accepts self-declaration for PHH applications and does not require a tehsildar income certificate for the standard PHH file). If applying under AAY, add the applicable criteria proof: widow certificate for widow AAY, disability certificate (40 percent or higher) for disability AAY, senior citizen ID for elderly AAY, or scheduled tribe certificate for tribal AAY in scheduled areas.

Bank and mobile linkage form the third layer. Bank account number and IFSC of the head of family for any DBT-linked scheme that rides on the ration card as an identity proof. Mobile number that will receive OTPs for e-KYC and status updates.

Optional documents that speed up verification are the previous ration card (if the household is applying for card renewal or splitting from a parent household), and the Aadhaar-Bank seeding letter (if applying with a bank that requires explicit NPCI mapping).

The department does not require caste certificate for a standard PHH application. Caste certificate is required only when applying under an AAY sub-category that draws on the scheduled tribe or scheduled caste criterion.

## How to apply for a Bihar ration card on epds.bihar.gov.in step by step

The Bihar EPDS portal is the single official entry point for a new ration card application. Follow these seven steps end to end.

1. Open epds.bihar.gov.in on a browser. On the home page, click Apply for Online RC. This opens the state's RCMS (Ration Card Management System) module.

2. Register on the portal. Enter your Aadhaar-linked mobile number, receive an OTP, verify it, and set a password. This creates your applicant login.

3. Log in and start a new application. Select the district, block, and gram panchayat (for rural) or ward (for urban) where the household resides. This routes the file to the correct block or urban local body.

4. Fill the household details form. Enter the head of family's name, Aadhaar number, date of birth, gender, occupation, and mobile number. Add every other household member with their Aadhaar number, date of birth, relationship to the head of family, and gender. Verify Aadhaar for each member through the inline e-KYC widget.

5. Upload documents. Family group photograph (JPEG under 200 KB), address proof (PDF or JPEG under 500 KB), and self-declaration of income on the state-prescribed format. If applying under AAY, upload the applicable criteria proof.

6. Select the card category (PHH or AAY or Anna Yojana pink) and preview the application. Cross-check every Aadhaar, date of birth, and spelling. Any mismatch triggers verification failure at the district office and adds 15 to 30 days to the timeline.

7. Submit the application. Note the acknowledgment number that the portal displays on submission. This is your reference number for every future status check, correction, or escalation. Save the acknowledgment PDF to your phone or print it.

Application processing at the block level is capped at 30 days under NFSA Section 14, though actual timelines run 15 to 45 days in most Bihar districts. If your file crosses 30 days without a decision, follow the escalation ladder in the grievance section below.

Offline application through the nearest FPS or the Block Supply Officer's office is also accepted for households without smartphone or internet access. The offline form is available at the block office free of cost, and the document stack is identical.

## How to check Bihar ration card status by application number or Aadhaar

Status checks on the Bihar EPDS portal work through three separate pathways, and each covers a different question.

By application reference number: on epds.bihar.gov.in, click RC Application Status on the home page, enter your acknowledgment number, and the portal returns the current stage (Received, Under Block Verification, Under District Verification, Approved, Rejected, Card Issued). This is the fastest route right after submission.

By Aadhaar number: on the national portal nfsa.gov.in, use the Know Your Ration Card tool. Enter your Aadhaar number and the captcha, and the system returns the ration card number and issuing state if one exists in the national NFSA database. Click through to epds.bihar.gov.in for the full state-level status.

By household head mobile number: on epds.bihar.gov.in, log in with the Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP, and the dashboard shows the household's card status, e-KYC compliance for every listed member, last three PDS transactions at the mapped FPS, and any pending grievances.

If none of the three pathways return a result, the application is either not yet keyed into the system by the block office (wait 7 to 10 days after submission), or the acknowledgment number was mistyped, or the Aadhaar is not yet linked in the district database. Retry after a week before treating a no-record response as concerning.

For files stuck beyond the 30-day NFSA statutory ceiling, file a formal grievance on the BPGRS portal or call 1800-345-6194 with the acknowledgment number.

## How to download your Bihar e-ration card via epds.bihar.gov.in, Mera Ration 2.0 and DigiLocker

The Bihar e-ration card, issued under the department's digitisation drive that runs on top of the NFSA near-100 percent digitisation baseline, is accepted as a valid ration document at every FPS across the state and every ONORC-integrated FPS across India. Three download routes work.

Route 1, epds.bihar.gov.in: log into the portal with your Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP, go to Download Ration Card, select your district, enter your ration card number, and save the PDF. This is the department-issued PDF and is the legally binding version if any discrepancy arises with the other two routes.

Route 2, Mera Ration 2.0 app: download the app from Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Log in with your Aadhaar number and verify the OTP. Select My Ration Card from the main menu, tap Download to save the PDF or Share to send via WhatsApp. Mera Ration 2.0 also supports biometric-authenticated portable withdrawal at any of the 5.44 lakh ONORC-integrated FPS across India, family management (add or remove member requests), digital surrender, and 13 regional languages including Hindi, Maithili, Bhojpuri (in progress), and English.

Route 3, DigiLocker: log into digilocker.gov.in with Aadhaar-mobile OTP. Search for Ration Card in Issued Documents, select Bihar as the state, and pull the state-issued PDF. Bihar is partially onboarded to DigiLocker for ration cards, so this route works for cards issued or re-issued after July 2023 but may not work for older legacy cards. If DigiLocker returns no record, fall back to Route 1 or Route 2.

All three downloads are free. Ignore any third-party app, cyber cafe, or website charging money for e-ration card download.

## The June-August 2026 clubbed distribution, and what to expect at your FPS

The Department of Food, Consumer Protection and Public Distribution announced that the monthly PDS quotas for June, July, and August 2026 will be released together in a single consolidated distribution window at every FPS across Bihar. The department released this decision in its May 2026 review meeting, per regional media coverage of the announcement.

The reason is flood-season supply logistics. Bihar's monsoon typically breaks in the second week of June and stresses road access to riverine districts through August. Muzaffarpur, Sitamarhi, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Saharsa, Katihar, Kishanganj, Araria, Purnia, and Supaul are the ten most flood-affected districts on the department's supply map. A single consolidated release lets the department pre-position the full three-month stock at every FPS in these districts before the roads become unreliable, and reduces the risk of a mid-monsoon supply gap that would cost the household its PMGKAY entitlement for the affected month.

What to expect at your FPS during the clubbed window. Every eligible household draws 15 kg of grain per person under PHH (5 kg for June, 5 kg for July, 5 kg for August), or 105 kg per household under AAY (35 kg for each of the three months), in a single visit. Aadhaar biometric authentication runs once for the combined draw, though the ePoS device may split the transaction receipt into three monthly entries for accounting.

Bring a larger cloth bag or two smaller bags to carry the consolidated quantum. If you cannot lift the full three-month draw in one visit, ask the FPS dealer to hold the balance for a second visit within 7 days. The department has instructed FPS dealers to allow split pickups within the same distribution window without a second biometric authentication.

If your FPS runs out of stock during the clubbed window or if the ePoS device is out of order for more than 3 days in a row, file a grievance on BPGRS or call 1800-345-6194. The department has committed to same-day escalation for clubbed-window supply gaps given the flood risk.

## Add or remove a family member on the Bihar ration card

Post-issuance member additions and removals are the most common ration-card operation on the EPDS portal after monthly PDS draw. Both operations are free and complete within 15 to 30 days.

Add a new member (newborn, spouse after marriage, elderly parent joining the household, other dependent). Log into epds.bihar.gov.in with Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP. Go to Add Member. Enter the new member's Aadhaar number, date of birth, relationship to head of family, and gender. Upload the supporting document: birth certificate for a newborn (issued by the municipal corporation, nagar panchayat, or gram panchayat), marriage certificate for a spouse (issued by the sub-registrar or under a religious authority), or Aadhaar and self-declaration for a joining elderly parent. Submit the request.

The addition is verified by the block office within 15 to 30 days. Aadhaar e-KYC of the added member is triggered automatically, so the newly added member must visit any FPS within 30 days of approval to complete biometric authentication on the ePoS device. Once e-KYC is done, the household's monthly PDS quantum increases by the added member's share from the next distribution cycle.

Remove a member (death in the family, marriage-out of the household, permanent relocation to another state, or member reaching age 18 and moving to a separate household). Log into epds.bihar.gov.in, go to Remove Member, select the member's name from the household list, choose the reason (deceased, married out, migrated, split household), upload the supporting proof (death certificate, marriage certificate, self-declaration with new-address proof, or split-household declaration), and submit. Removal is processed within 15 to 30 days. The remaining household continues to draw the reduced per-person entitlement from the next cycle.

If a member has been deceased for more than 6 months and the death was not reported to the department, the household may receive a suspension notice from the ONORC deduplication engine that catches Aadhaar-death linkage. File the removal request immediately with a copy of the death certificate to avoid card suspension.

## Correction, surrender and transfer on the Bihar portal

Four other post-issuance operations round out the EPDS module, and all four are free.

Name spelling or date-of-birth correction. Log into epds.bihar.gov.in, go to Correction, upload the corrected supporting document (Aadhaar for name spelling, birth certificate or matric marksheet for date of birth), and submit. Correction is validated within 3 to 7 days and reflects on the card at the next state portal refresh cycle.

Address change within Bihar. Log into the portal, go to Address Change, select the new district and block or ward, upload the new address proof (electricity bill, rent agreement, or municipal water bill in the head of family's name), and submit. The change is verified by the new block office within 15 to 30 days, and the household is re-mapped to the nearest FPS at the new address.

Surrender the ration card. Surrender is used when the entire household is moving permanently out of Bihar, or if the household's income has risen above the PHH ceiling on the state priority-scoring model, or if the household voluntarily wants to exit the PDS. Log into the portal, go to Surrender, submit the state-prescribed self-declaration, and the card is cancelled within 15 days. Surrender frees the beneficiary slot for a new applicant on the state PHH waitlist.

Transfer the ration card to another state. The formal route is to surrender the Bihar card and apply fresh in the new state. Practically, ONORC lets a migrant draw ration in any state without transferring the card, so if the move is temporary (work assignment, seasonal migration, extended family stay), keep the Bihar card active and draw at the ONORC-integrated FPS in the new state. Transfer through surrender is the correct route only for permanent relocation with full family.

All four operations are free through the state portal. Ignore any cyber cafe or private agent charging money.

## Grievance and helplines, 1800-345-6194, 1967 and BPGRS online portal

The Department of Food, Consumer Protection and Public Distribution runs a multi-channel grievance mechanism, and NFSA Section 25 mandates a two-level redress system with the District Grievance Redressal Officer at the first level and the State Food Commission at the second level.

Department toll-free helpline: 1800-345-6194 (Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 6 PM). Use this for card status escalations beyond 30 days, FPS malpractice complaints, ePoS device downtime, e-KYC blockers, and clubbed-window supply gap issues.

All-India food and PDS helpline: 1967. This is the national NFSA helpline and works in Bihar. It is a good fallback if 1800-345-6194 is not reachable, or for questions about ONORC portability that touch multiple states.

BPGRS (Bihar Public Grievance Redressal System) portal: file an online grievance at the BPGRS portal, attach your acknowledgment number or ration card number, and select the Food and Civil Supplies category. Grievances filed on BPGRS carry a statutory 60-day response deadline under the Bihar Right to Public Services Act, and repeated non-response can be escalated to the State Public Grievance Redressal Commissioner.

Consumer Helpline for FPS malpractice: 1915 or consumerhelpline.gov.in. Use this if the FPS dealer is short-weighing the distribution, refusing to draw the full quantum, demanding cash payment for a free PMGKAY draw, or refusing to run e-KYC.

Escalation ladder for a stalled ration card application in Bihar. Step 1: file a grievance on BPGRS with the acknowledgment number, wait 15 days. Step 2: escalate to the Block Supply Officer at the block office with a copy of the BPGRS complaint, wait 15 days. Step 3: escalate to the District Supply Officer (DSO) at the district collectorate, wait 15 days. Step 4: escalate to the Bihar State Food Commission with all prior grievance copies, which has statutory power under NFSA Section 16 to direct the department to act. Step 5: file a Right to Information (RTI) application with the DSO asking for the status and the reason for the delay. The RTI response often unblocks the file within 30 days.

## Related schemes for Bihar ration card holders, PMGKAY, ONORC, e-Shram, PM-JAY, PM-KISAN

The ration card in Bihar acts as an identity spine for several other central and state schemes. Cross-linking your card to the following programmes multiplies its value.

PMGKAY (Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana): this is the free-grain layer sitting on top of NFSA. Every PHH member gets 5 kg per month at zero cost, and every AAY household gets 35 kg per month at zero cost, till 31 December 2028 per the Union Cabinet decision of 29 November 2023. No separate application is needed. If your ration card is active in Bihar, you draw PMGKAY automatically. See our [PMGKAY guide](/sarkari-yojana/pradhan-mantri-garib-kalyan-anna-yojana) for the full quantum, price, and fortified rice rollout.

ONORC (One Nation One Ration Card): portability layer that lets any Bihar ration card holder draw at any of the 5.44 lakh FPS across India using Aadhaar biometric on the ePoS. Especially useful for Bihar migrant workers in Delhi, Mumbai, Ludhiana, Surat, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Kolkata. See our [ration card 2026 hub](/sarkari-yojana/ration-card-2026) for the ONORC 100 crore transactions milestone and the state-wise ONORC status.

e-Shram: national database of unorganised workers, and Bihar ration card holders in the informal sector (agriculture, construction, domestic work, street vending) should register at eshram.gov.in with their Aadhaar to receive the e-Shram Universal Account Number (UAN) card. The UAN links to future welfare payouts and to the ration card for cross-verification.

PM-JAY (Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana): free health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year at any empanelled hospital. Bihar households eligible under the SECC 2011 database (which overlaps significantly with the state's PHH priority-scoring model) automatically qualify. Check eligibility at pmjay.gov.in with your Aadhaar or ration card number. See our [PM-JAY guide](/sarkari-yojana/pradhan-mantri-jan-arogya-yojana) for the empanelment list.

PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi): Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 to every eligible landholding farmer family, credited directly to the Aadhaar-seeded bank account. Bihar has one of the highest PM-KISAN beneficiary counts nationally. Ration card is not the primary eligibility document (land record is), but the ration card is often used to verify household composition during the state-level scrutiny. See our [PM-KISAN guide](/sarkari-yojana/pm-kisan-samman-nidhi-yojana).

Bihar-specific state schemes that use the ration card as an identity anchor include the state's kerosene distribution (in blocks that still receive PDS kerosene), the Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana verification (which cross-checks household composition), and the state pension schemes (which use the ration card for widow and elderly identification).

## Frequently asked questions

**How to apply for Bihar ration card online in 2026?**

Apply on epds.bihar.gov.in. Register with your Aadhaar-linked mobile number and verify OTP. Select your district, block, and gram panchayat or ward. Fill the household form with the Aadhaar of every listed member. Upload family group photograph, address proof, and the state-prescribed self-declaration of income. Select the card category (PHH, AAY, or Anna Yojana pink), submit, and save the acknowledgment number. Processing is capped at 30 days under NFSA Section 14. If stuck beyond 30 days, file a grievance on BPGRS or call 1800-345-6194.

**What is the e-KYC deadline for Bihar ration card in 2026?**

The Department of Food, Consumer Protection and Public Distribution set 31 March 2026 as the hard deadline for Aadhaar e-KYC of every listed member above age 5. 5.2 crore holders completed e-KYC by the deadline, but 1.65 crore holders are still pending as of the department's May 2026 review. Pending households face suspension risk on the next distribution cycle. Late e-KYC is accepted free of cost at any FPS with an ePoS device.

**How to check Bihar ration card status on epds.bihar.gov.in?**

On epds.bihar.gov.in, click RC Application Status on the home page, enter your acknowledgment number, and view the current stage (Received, Under Block Verification, Under District Verification, Approved, Rejected, Card Issued). Alternately, log in with your Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP and check the household dashboard for card status, e-KYC compliance, and last three transactions. For a no-record response, wait 7 to 10 days after submission before treating it as concerning.

On the Mera Ration 2.0 app, log in with Aadhaar OTP, select My Ration Card, and tap Download. On DigiLocker, log in and search Ration Card under Issued Documents (works for Bihar cards issued after July 2023). All three routes are free. Any charge by a cyber cafe or third party is unauthorised.

**What documents are needed for a new Bihar ration card?**

Aadhaar of every household member, one address proof (voter ID, electricity bill, rent agreement, or municipal water bill), family group photograph, and state-prescribed self-declaration of income. Bihar accepts self-declaration and does not require a tehsildar income certificate for standard PHH files. If applying under AAY, add the applicable criteria proof (widow certificate, disability certificate, senior citizen ID, or scheduled tribe certificate). Add bank account number and IFSC for DBT-linked schemes.

**What happens if I missed the Bihar e-KYC deadline of 31 March 2026?**

The card is flagged for suspension risk, and the ePoS at the FPS may block your monthly draw until every listed member above age 5 completes Aadhaar e-KYC. Late e-KYC is accepted free of cost. Take every pending member to your FPS with their original Aadhaar during working hours, ask the dealer to run fingerprint or iris or OTP e-KYC on the ePoS, and collect the acknowledgment slip. Reactivation reflects within 48 to 72 hours. If the FPS refuses, escalate to the Block Supply Officer or call 1800-345-6194.

**How to add a new family member to my Bihar ration card?**

Log into epds.bihar.gov.in with Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP, go to Add Member, enter the new member's Aadhaar number, date of birth, relationship to head of family, and gender. Upload the supporting document (birth certificate for a newborn, marriage certificate for a spouse, Aadhaar and self-declaration for a joining elderly parent). Submit. Addition is verified by the block office within 15 to 30 days, and the added member's e-KYC is triggered automatically. The household's PDS quantum increases from the next distribution cycle.

**What is the Bihar ration card helpline number?**

Two toll-free numbers work. The department's own helpline is 1800-345-6194, operating Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 6 PM. Use this for card status escalations, FPS malpractice, ePoS issues, and e-KYC blockers. The all-India food and PDS helpline 1967 also works in Bihar and is a good fallback. For online grievance filing, use the Bihar Public Grievance Redressal System (BPGRS) portal, which carries a 60-day statutory response deadline under the state's Right to Public Services Act.

**What is the Anna Yojana pink card in Bihar?**

Anna Yojana pink card is Bihar's state-level overlay on top of central NFSA classification. The state government rolled out the pink card to extend PDS coverage to households ranking just below the NFSA cutoff on the state priority-scoring model but flagged as vulnerable by the district administration. Pink card households draw a state-notified grain quantum funded partly by the state exchequer and partly through the NFSA channel. Issuance is demand-based through the block office and is not uniform across all Bihar districts.

**Why was the June-August 2026 Bihar ration distribution clubbed together?**

The Department of Food, Consumer Protection and Public Distribution clubbed the June, July, and August 2026 monthly quotas into a single consolidated distribution window because of flood-season supply logistics. Bihar's monsoon typically stresses road access to riverine districts (Muzaffarpur, Sitamarhi, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Saharsa, Katihar, Kishanganj, Araria, Purnia, Supaul) from mid-June through August. A single release lets the department pre-position the full three-month stock at every FPS before roads become unreliable, and prevents mid-monsoon supply gaps that would otherwise cost the household its PMGKAY entitlement.

If applying under AAY, add the applicable criteria proof (widow certificate, disability certificate, senior citizen ID, or scheduled tribe certificate). Add bank account number and IFSC for DBT-linked schemes.
faqs.question: What documents are needed for a new Bihar ration card?

faqs.answer: The card is flagged for suspension risk, and the ePoS at the FPS may block your monthly draw until every listed member above age 5 completes Aadhaar e-KYC. Late e-KYC is accepted free of cost. Take every pending member to your FPS with their original Aadhaar during working hours, ask the dealer to run fingerprint or iris or OTP e-KYC on the ePoS, and collect the acknowledgment slip. Reactivation reflects within 48 to 72 hours. If the FPS refuses, escalate to the Block Supply Officer or call 1800-345-6194.
faqs.question: What happens if I missed the Bihar e-KYC deadline of 31 March 2026?

faqs.answer: Log into epds.bihar.gov.in with Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP, go to Add Member, enter the new member's Aadhaar number, date of birth, relationship to head of family, and gender. Upload the supporting document (birth certificate for a newborn, marriage certificate for a spouse, Aadhaar and self-declaration for a joining elderly parent). Submit. Addition is verified by the block office within 15 to 30 days, and the added member's e-KYC is triggered automatically. The household's PDS quantum increases from the next distribution cycle.
faqs.question: How to add a new family member to my Bihar ration card?

faqs.answer: Two toll-free numbers work. The department's own helpline is 1800-345-6194, operating Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 6 PM. Use this for card status escalations, FPS malpractice, ePoS issues, and e-KYC blockers. The all-India food and PDS helpline 1967 also works in Bihar and is a good fallback. For online grievance filing, use the Bihar Public Grievance Redressal System (BPGRS) portal, which carries a 60-day statutory response deadline under the state's Right to Public Services Act.
faqs.question: What is the Bihar ration card helpline number?

faqs.answer: Anna Yojana pink card is Bihar's state-level overlay on top of central NFSA classification. The state government rolled out the pink card to extend PDS coverage to households ranking just below the NFSA cutoff on the state priority-scoring model but flagged as vulnerable by the district administration. Pink card households draw a state-notified grain quantum funded partly by the state exchequer and partly through the NFSA channel. Issuance is demand-based through the block office and is not uniform across all Bihar districts.
faqs.question: What is the Anna Yojana pink card in Bihar?

faqs.answer: The Department of Food, Consumer Protection and Public Distribution clubbed the June, July, and August 2026 monthly quotas into a single consolidated distribution window because of flood-season supply logistics. Bihar's monsoon typically stresses road access to riverine districts (Muzaffarpur, Sitamarhi, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Saharsa, Katihar, Kishanganj, Araria, Purnia, Supaul) from mid-June through August. A single release lets the department pre-position the full three-month stock at every FPS before roads become unreliable, and prevents mid-monsoon supply gaps that would otherwise cost the household its PMGKAY entitlement.
faqs.question: Why was the June-August 2026 Bihar ration distribution clubbed together?

content:
## Delhi ration card 2026 at a glance

The Delhi ration card is the household identity document issued by the Department of Food, Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD) that lets a family draw free wheat, rice, and sugar from the Public Distribution System (PDS) at any Fair Price Shop (FPS) in the state. Two very fresh policy shifts have made 2026 the most active year for new applications in more than a decade.

First, Delhi resumed large-scale ration card issuance on 15 May 2026 after a 13-year gap. The freeze had been in place since 2013 when the state hit its central National Food Security Act (NFSA) beneficiary cap, and Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced during the relaunch that 2 lakh new ration cards would be issued in FY26 after the state cancelled 7.72 lakh bogus cards during a cleanup drive, per PIB reporting on the Delhi Food Department press briefing.

Second, the Delhi Food Security (Amendment) Rules 2026 raised the annual household income ceiling for a Priority Household ration card from Rs 1.20 lakh to Rs 2.50 lakh, effective 13 July 2026 per the GNCTD gazette notification. This is the single biggest income-slab change in Delhi's PDS history and brings roughly 4 lakh additional households into the eligibility net that were previously above the earlier ceiling.

The Delhi PDS now covers 72.78 lakh beneficiaries across 17.79 lakh ration cards, distributed through 1,995 Fair Price Shops in the state, per the latest Department of Food, Supplies and Consumer Affairs data cited in the 15 May 2026 press briefing. Biometric ePoS devices are mandatory at every FPS since the 2025 mandate, and electronic weighing machines have been rolled out at all shops to eliminate the short-weighing complaints that dominated grievance filings in the earlier decade.

If you were denied a Delhi ration card between 2013 and 2024 because the state had frozen issuance, or if your household income falls between Rs 1.20 lakh and Rs 2.50 lakh per year, 2026 is the year to reapply. This page walks through the eligibility rules, the three card types, the freshness moats, the document checklist, the seven-step online application flow, and the grievance escalation ladder.

## Who is eligible for a Delhi ration card in 2026

Eligibility for a Delhi Priority Household ration card is set by the Delhi Food Security (Amendment) Rules 2026, and the rules combine an income ceiling with a set of exclusion criteria.

The income ceiling is Rs 2.50 lakh per household per year, effective 13 July 2026. This was raised from the earlier Rs 1.20 lakh per year cap that had been in force since 2013. The household income is calculated across all earning members and includes salary, business income, agricultural income, pension, and rental income. Self-declaration is accepted at the application stage, with the district office reserving the right to verify against income tax records.

The Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) criteria are separate from the PHH income ceiling and use inclusion tests rather than a rupee cap. AAY covers households of widows without an earning member, disabled persons where the primary earner is disabled with no alternate earning member, elderly above age 60 with no earning support, tribal households in scheduled areas, and destitute households identified by the district magistrate. Delhi runs about 68,000 AAY cards.

Exclusion criteria are the flip side and apply across both AAY and PHH categories. Households that filed an income tax return in the previous financial year are excluded. Households owning a four-wheeler passenger vehicle (excluding autos, commercial goods vehicles, and taxis) registered in an adult member's name are excluded. Households with an existing active ration card in any other state are excluded, since the One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) database catches the duplicate. Households where any adult member is a government employee drawing salary above the notified threshold are excluded.

Nationality is Indian citizen only. Every household member above age 5 must complete Aadhaar e-KYC. The e-KYC deadline in Delhi was 31 December 2025 for existing cardholders, and any card without completed e-KYC as of July 2026 is either suspended or on the suspension watchlist. The Department has extended the e-KYC compliance drive through the FPS network, so any suspended card can be reactivated free of cost at any ePoS-equipped FPS by taking the household Aadhaars during working hours.

## Types of ration cards in Delhi

Delhi runs three ration card categories in 2026, and picking the right one at the application stage avoids rejection cycles.

Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) is the poorest-of-poor slab. Eligibility uses inclusion criteria (widow-headed household, disabled primary earner, elderly with no support, tribal household, destitute) rather than an income ceiling. AAY draws 35 kg of grain per household per month, free under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY). Delhi runs roughly 68,000 AAY cards.

Priority (PR) is the main NFSA slab, funded by the central NFSA allocation. Eligibility is set by the Rs 2.50 lakh per year income ceiling combined with the exclusion criteria. PR cards draw 5 kg of grain per person per month, free under PMGKAY. Delhi runs roughly 17.05 lakh PR cards as of the 15 May 2026 press briefing.

Priority-State (PR-S) is Delhi's own state-pool card, funded by the GNCTD budget for households that qualify on the income and exclusion criteria but fall outside the central NFSA cap. PR-S cards get the same 5 kg per person per month entitlement as PR cards, and the state pays the differential subsidy from its own budget. This is the slab that most of the 2 lakh new cards announced for FY26 will land in, since the central NFSA cap for Delhi is largely filled by existing PR cards. Delhi runs roughly 65,000 PR-S cards, and the number is expected to cross 2 lakh by end-FY26 as the fresh issuance drive rolls out.

If you are applying fresh in 2026 and your income is below Rs 2.50 lakh per year, the district office typically issues a PR card if the central cap has room and a PR-S card if it does not. You do not choose the slab at application, the department slots you based on the current pool availability. The entitlement (5 kg per person per month, free grain under PMGKAY) is identical across PR and PR-S.

## The 13-year freeze that ended 15 May 2026: what changed and how to apply now

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced on 15 May 2026 that the Delhi government has resumed large-scale issuance of new ration cards after a gap of 13 years, and 2 lakh new cards will be issued in FY26 to cover households that were denied cards during the freeze period, per PIB reporting on the Delhi Food Department press briefing.

The freeze traces back to 2013 when Delhi hit its central NFSA beneficiary cap and the state stopped taking new applications for the PR slab. Between 2013 and 2024, only a trickle of fresh cards were issued to replace deceased-member deletions, and the majority of new-to-Delhi households (migrants, newly married, newborn-added families beyond the cap) were unable to secure a card. The state's PR-S pool absorbed a small share, but the state budget commitment was capped at roughly 65,000 households.

Three enabling actions preceded the 15 May 2026 relaunch. First, the state ran a cleanup drive that cancelled 7.72 lakh bogus cards over 2024-25, using the ePoS transaction data cross-linked to Aadhaar e-KYC and ONORC deduplication. Deceased-member cards that had not been reported, income tax filer households, four-wheeler owners, and duplicate-state entries were the four cancellation categories. Second, biometric ePoS devices were made mandatory at every FPS in the state, eliminating manual sign-off and cutting theft. Third, electronic weighing machines were rolled out at all 1,995 FPS to end short-weighing complaints.

The 2 lakh fresh cards announced for FY26 will be issued through the standard online application flow on nfs.delhigovt.nic.in and edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in. Priority is being given to households that (a) applied between 2013 and 2024 and were denied due to the freeze, (b) fall within the newly raised Rs 2.50 lakh income ceiling, and (c) have completed Aadhaar e-KYC for every listed member above age 5. If you were denied earlier and your acknowledgment number is still on record, the department is auto-pulling those files first; if not, submit a fresh application and note the acknowledgment number for tracking.

## Income cap raised from Rs 1.20 lakh to Rs 2.50 lakh on 13 July 2026

The Delhi Food Security (Amendment) Rules 2026 raised the annual household income ceiling for a Priority Household ration card from Rs 1.20 lakh to Rs 2.50 lakh, effective 13 July 2026 per the GNCTD gazette notification issued by the Department of Food, Supplies and Consumer Affairs. This is 10 days old as of publish, and no other state has revised its income ceiling in 2026.

The rationale for the revision was that the earlier Rs 1.20 lakh ceiling, unchanged since 2013, was well below Delhi's household income distribution and was leaving a wide band of low-income households (roughly Rs 1.20 lakh to Rs 2.50 lakh per year) outside the PR eligibility net. With Delhi's cost of living having risen roughly 90 percent over 2013 to 2026 per Reserve Bank of India CPI-Delhi data, the earlier ceiling had become effectively obsolete, and the amendment resets the eligibility net to reflect current household economics.

For existing PR-S applicants, the amendment matters in two ways. First, PR-S cards issued to households in the Rs 1.20 lakh to Rs 2.50 lakh income band before 13 July 2026 are now within the newly raised PR ceiling. The department is running a conversion drive where these PR-S cards may be reclassified to PR (central NFSA) as central cap headroom becomes available, without any action required from the cardholder. Second, applications that were rejected between 2013 and 13 July 2026 solely for exceeding the Rs 1.20 lakh ceiling but were within Rs 2.50 lakh should be resubmitted, and the department is running a fast-track review for these files.

For fresh applicants, the amendment expands the eligible household base by roughly 4 lakh households per department estimates cited in the gazette notification. If your household income is between Rs 1.20 lakh and Rs 2.50 lakh per year, you are now eligible where you were previously excluded. The application flow is unchanged, but the income declaration form now uses the Rs 2.50 lakh ceiling as the PR threshold.

The Rs 2.50 lakh ceiling is also higher than Uttar Pradesh's Rs 2 lakh rural and matches the Rs 3 lakh urban only partially, so cross-state migrants moving to Delhi from UP now benefit from a broader eligibility net if they apply fresh in Delhi rather than porting their UP card under ONORC.

## Documents required for a Delhi ration card

The Delhi document checklist has three layers, and getting all three ready before starting the online application saves the most common cause of file rejection.

Identity and address proofs form the base. Aadhaar card of every household member is mandatory (children under age 5 exempt from Aadhaar, but Aadhaar is preferred where available). One address proof in the name of the head of family from voter ID, electricity bill, water bill, telephone bill, gas connection book, rent agreement registered with the sub-registrar, or a residence certificate from the SDM. Passport-size family group photograph showing all listed members together.

Income and eligibility proofs form the second layer. Income declaration form filled by the head of family stating annual household income below Rs 2.50 lakh (self-declaration is accepted, but false declaration attracts prosecution under NFSA Section 32). If applying under the AAY slab, add the applicable criteria proof: widow certificate for widow-headed household, disability certificate above 40 percent for disabled primary earner, senior citizen ID for elderly-headed households, and SC/ST certificate for tribal households.

Bank and mobile linkage forms the third layer. Bank account number and IFSC of the head of family from any nationalised or scheduled commercial bank (Delhi state cooperative bank accounts also accepted). Aadhaar-seeded mobile number for OTP-based verification during the online flow. This mobile number is also used for status updates and grievance callbacks, so use the number you actively check.

Special-case documents apply in three scenarios. For newborns being added to an existing card, birth certificate from the municipal corporation. For new brides being added, marriage certificate from the sub-registrar or the applicable religious authority. For household members returning from long-term migration, self-declaration plus previous address proof.

All uploads on nfs.delhigovt.nic.in and edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in accept PDF or JPEG under 2 MB per file. Keep the originals with you for the district office verification visit, which happens within 15 to 30 days of application submission.

## How to apply for a Delhi ration card on nfs.delhigovt.nic.in step by step

The Delhi online application flow runs on two portals: nfs.delhigovt.nic.in for the ration card creation form itself, and edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in for the linked citizen services (address verification, income certificate download, income declaration). The seven-step flow below is the fastest path.

Step 1: Register on edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in with your mobile number and verify OTP. This creates your Delhi Citizen ID, which is required for any government service application in the state. If you already have an e-District account, log in with your credentials.

Step 2: Complete the Aadhaar e-KYC of the head of family on the e-District portal. Enter your Aadhaar number, verify the OTP sent to the Aadhaar-linked mobile, and confirm your demographic details. This links your e-District account to the central Aadhaar database and pre-fills subsequent forms.

Step 3: Navigate to nfs.delhigovt.nic.in from the e-District portal (or open it directly and log in with the same credentials). Select Apply for New Ration Card from the main menu.

Step 4: Fill the household details form. Enter the head of family's name, Aadhaar, date of birth, and relationship (self). Add every household member one at a time with their name, Aadhaar, date of birth, and relationship to head of family. Aadhaar e-KYC is triggered for each member above age 5, so all members must be available for OTP verification during the session.

Step 5: Upload the document set. Aadhaar of each member (or the e-KYC confirmation for those verified in Step 4), one address proof, family group photograph, income declaration form filled and signed. If applying under AAY, add the applicable criteria proof.

Step 6: Fill the bank details section with account number, IFSC, and account holder name. Submit the application and note the acknowledgment number that appears on the confirmation screen. Save a PDF copy of the confirmation for your records.

Step 7: Track the application on nfs.delhigovt.nic.in under Track Application using the acknowledgment number. The district office runs a physical verification visit within 15 to 30 days, and the card is issued within 30 to 60 days of submission. You will receive an SMS on the registered mobile when the card is ready for digital download and physical delivery.

Offline application through the nearest FPS or the Food and Civil Supplies office in your district is also allowed, with the same form and document set. Offline is slower (typically 60 to 90 days) but works for applicants without internet access.

## How to check Delhi ration card status by application number or Aadhaar

Status checks work through three routes on the Delhi portal, and each route surfaces different data.

By application number (recommended for fresh applicants): visit nfs.delhigovt.nic.in, click Track Application on the main menu, enter your acknowledgment number, and view the current status. The dashboard shows five possible states: Received (form submitted), Under Verification (district office reviewing), Verification Complete (physical visit done), Approved (card being printed), and Issued (ready for download or delivery). If the status shows Rejected, click through to the reason code and follow the appeal instructions.

By Aadhaar number (for existing cardholders or applicants who lost the acknowledgment): visit nfs.delhigovt.nic.in, click Know Your Ration Card, enter your Aadhaar number and the captcha. The system returns the ration card number if one exists in the Delhi database, along with the card type (AAY, PR, PR-S), the FPS assigned, and the last three PDS transactions.

By head-of-family mobile number: visit nfs.delhigovt.nic.in, click Login, enter the Aadhaar-seeded mobile number of the head of family, verify OTP. The dashboard shows the household card details, e-KYC compliance status for each member, and the monthly PDS entitlement history for the last 12 months.

If none of the three routes returns a result, the application is either not yet keyed into the system by the district office (wait 7 to 10 days after submission before treating a no-record response as concerning), or the acknowledgment number was mistyped. For applications pending beyond the 30-day NFSA statutory ceiling, file a formal grievance on nfs.delhigovt.nic.in under Grievance, or call 1031 (Delhi grievance helpline) or 1800-11-0841 (department toll-free).

## How to download your Delhi e-ration card

The Delhi e-ration card is legally equivalent to the physical card at every FPS in the state and is accepted for portable withdrawal at any ONORC-integrated FPS across India. Three download routes work.

State portal (recommended for the authoritative copy): log into nfs.delhigovt.nic.in with your Aadhaar-seeded mobile OTP or your e-District Citizen ID credentials. Navigate to Download e-Ration Card. Select the current year and click Generate PDF. Save the PDF to your device. This is the legally issued document and takes precedence over any other copy if there is a discrepancy.

Mera Ration 2.0 app (recommended for portable withdrawal and family management): download the Mera Ration 2.0 app from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Log in with your Aadhaar number and verify OTP. Select My Ration Card. The app displays the Delhi household card with all listed members, the assigned FPS, and the monthly entitlement. Tap Download to save the PDF or Share to send via WhatsApp. The app also supports biometric-authenticated portable withdrawal at any ONORC-integrated FPS, digital add or remove member requests, digital surrender, and transaction history.

DigiLocker (recommended for archival and cross-service use): log into digilocker.gov.in with your Aadhaar-mobile OTP. Search for Ration Card in the Issued Documents section, select Delhi as the issuing state, and pull the PDF. Delhi is one of the fully onboarded states for DigiLocker ration cards, so this route works reliably. The DigiLocker PDF carries a QR code that any verifier can scan to confirm authenticity.

All three downloads are free. Ignore any third-party app or website charging a fee for Delhi e-ration card download. If your card is not yet issued (status shows Under Verification or Approved but not Issued), the download will fail on all three routes until the district office marks the card as Issued.

## Add or remove a family member on the Delhi ration card

Post-issuance updates to the family list are done through nfs.delhigovt.nic.in and take 15 to 30 days for the district office to process.

To add a new member (newborn, spouse after marriage, elderly parent joining the household): log into nfs.delhigovt.nic.in with the head-of-family Aadhaar OTP. Navigate to Add Member. Enter the new member's Aadhaar number, name, date of birth, and relationship to head of family. Upload the supporting document (birth certificate from the municipal corporation for a newborn, marriage certificate from the sub-registrar for a spouse, Aadhaar plus self-declaration for an elderly parent). Submit. Aadhaar e-KYC of the added member is triggered automatically, so the new member must be available for OTP verification during the session. The addition is verified by the district office within 15 to 30 days, and the updated card is available for download from the state portal once the addition is processed.

To remove a member (death, marriage-out of the household, permanent migration out of Delhi): log into nfs.delhigovt.nic.in, navigate to Remove Member, select the member's name from the dropdown of listed members, choose the reason (deceased, married out, migrated out of Delhi, other), and upload the supporting proof (death certificate from the municipal corporation, marriage certificate, self-declaration for migration). Submit. Removal is processed within 15 to 30 days. The remaining household continues to draw the reduced per-person entitlement.

For newborn additions specifically, Delhi runs a fast-track process where the addition can be initiated at the delivery hospital itself if the hospital is empanelled under the Delhi Arogya Kosh. The hospital submits the newborn Aadhaar-enrolment form and the ration card add-member form together, and the addition is processed within 7 to 15 days.

Both operations are free of cost. Ignore any private agent charging money for these services.

## Correction, surrender and transfer on the Delhi portal

Corrections to the card details cover four common scenarios and are done through nfs.delhigovt.nic.in.

Name spelling or date-of-birth correction: log in, navigate to Correction, select the field to correct (name, date of birth, gender, relationship), upload the supporting document (corrected Aadhaar, birth certificate, matric marksheet), submit. Correction is processed within 3 to 7 days and reflects on the card once approved. Fee is Rs 10 per correction.

Address change within Delhi: log in, navigate to Change Address, enter the new address (house number, street, colony, PIN code), upload the new address proof (voter ID, electricity bill, water bill, rent agreement). Submit. The change is verified by the district office of the new address within 15 to 30 days, and the assigned FPS is updated to the FPS covering the new address.

Surrender the ration card: surrender is done when the entire household is moving out of Delhi permanently, or when the household income rises above the Rs 2.50 lakh Priority Household ceiling and the card is no longer eligible. Log in, navigate to Surrender, submit self-declaration with the reason. The card is cancelled within 15 days. Failure to surrender an ineligible card is a violation under NFSA Section 32 and can attract penalty.

Transfer out of Delhi to another state: there is no direct transfer flow. The household applies fresh in the new state, and once the new card is issued, the ONORC deduplication engine auto-cancels the Delhi card. During the transition period (typically 30 to 60 days), the household can still draw ration in either state under ONORC portability. Do not surrender the Delhi card before the new state card is issued, or the household loses PDS access in the interim.

All corrections and surrender are free except the Rs 10 name-correction fee.

## Grievance and helplines: 1800-11-0841 and 1031

The Department of Food, Supplies and Consumer Affairs runs a two-level grievance mechanism under NFSA Section 25, with a District Grievance Redressal Officer at the first level and the Delhi State Food Commission at the second level.

Primary helpline numbers. 1800-11-0841 is the department toll-free helpline for ration card queries, application status, e-KYC issues, and FPS complaints. Available Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 5 PM. 1031 is the Delhi Government citizen grievance helpline covering all state services including PDS. Available 24 hours. Both numbers are free from any phone in Delhi.

Online grievance filing on nfs.delhigovt.nic.in under the Grievance section. Fill the grievance form with your ration card number or acknowledgment number, describe the issue, upload any supporting document (screenshot, photo, notice copy), submit. The system generates a grievance reference number. First response is within 7 days, and resolution is committed within 15 days.

Escalation ladder for unresolved issues. Step 1: file a written grievance on the state portal, keep the reference number, wait 15 days. Step 2: escalate to the District Supply Officer (DSO) of your district by email or in person with a copy of the portal grievance and the reference number, wait 15 days. Step 3: escalate to the Delhi State Food Commission, which has statutory power under NFSA Section 16 to direct the department to act. The Commission's office is at Vikas Bhawan, Delhi. Step 4: file a Right to Information (RTI) application with the DSO office asking for the status and reason for the delay. RTI responses within 30 days often unblock stalled files.

For FPS-specific complaints (short-weighing, dealer not opening the shop, refusing to give the entitled quantum, demanding extra payment), call 1800-11-0841 or use the Consumer Helpline at 1915 (consumerhelpline.gov.in). The department also runs a WhatsApp grievance channel; the number is displayed at every FPS on the mandatory citizen information board.

## Related schemes for Delhi ration card holders

The Delhi ration card is the household identity anchor for a set of related central and state welfare schemes, and cross-linking the card unlocks a broader benefit stack.

Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) is the free-grain top-up that funds the 5 kg per person per month for PR and PR-S cardholders and the 35 kg per household per month for AAY cardholders. The scheme runs through 31 December 2028 per the Union Cabinet decision of 29 November 2023 with a five-year outlay of Rs 11.80 lakh crore. Read the full [PMGKAY guide and eligibility rules](/sarkari-yojana/pmgkay-2026) for the national picture.

One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) lets Delhi cardholders draw their monthly entitlement at any of the 5.44 lakh ONORC-integrated Fair Price Shops across India. This is critical for Delhi's large migrant population who visit home states seasonally. Portability works through Aadhaar biometric authentication on the ePoS at any integrated FPS. See the [ONORC portability rules and Mera Ration 2.0 guide](/sarkari-yojana/onorc-2026) for full details.

Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) or Ayushman Bharat provides Rs 5 lakh per family per year of secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation coverage. Delhi PR and PR-S cardholders in the SECC 2011 database are auto-eligible, and the ration card acts as the household identity proof at the empanelled hospital. See the [PM-JAY eligibility and hospital list guide](/sarkari-yojana/ayushman-bharat-2026) for enrolment steps.

e-Shram is the national unorganised worker registry, and the ration card is one of the accepted identity proofs for e-Shram registration. Delhi has 51 lakh unorganised workers registered on e-Shram as of 2026, and the ration card is used as the household proof for the linked Rs 2 lakh accidental death and disability insurance under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana. See the [e-Shram registration guide](/sarkari-yojana/e-shram-2026) for the flow.

State-level overlays include the Delhi Ladli scheme (for girl children in ration card households), the Delhi Widow Pension (linked to the ration card as household proof), and the Delhi Old Age Pension (for elderly members listed on the ration card). Each of these schemes uses the ration card as the primary household identity proof at the application stage.

## Frequently asked questions

**How to apply for Delhi ration card online in 2026?**

Register on edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in with your mobile number and verify OTP, then navigate to nfs.delhigovt.nic.in and select Apply for New Ration Card. Fill the household details form with the Aadhaar of every listed member, upload one address proof, family group photograph, and the income declaration form stating household income below Rs 2.50 lakh per year, add bank account details, and submit. Note the acknowledgment number for tracking. The district office runs a physical verification visit within 15 to 30 days, and the card is issued within 30 to 60 days of submission.

**What is the income limit for a Delhi ration card in 2026?**

The income limit for a Delhi Priority Household ration card is Rs 2.50 lakh per household per year, raised from Rs 1.20 lakh via the Delhi Food Security (Amendment) Rules 2026 effective 13 July 2026. Household income is calculated across all earning members and includes salary, business income, agricultural income, pension, and rental income. Self-declaration is accepted at the application stage, with the district office reserving the right to verify against income tax records. AAY eligibility uses inclusion criteria (widow, disabled, elderly with no support, tribal, destitute) rather than an income ceiling.

**When did Delhi start issuing new ration cards again after the 13-year freeze?**

Delhi resumed large-scale ration card issuance on 15 May 2026, after a 13-year gap since 2013 when the state hit its central NFSA beneficiary cap. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced during the relaunch that 2 lakh new ration cards will be issued in FY26. This followed a cleanup drive that cancelled 7.72 lakh bogus cards across 2024-25, biometric ePoS mandate at every FPS, and rollout of electronic weighing machines at all 1,995 FPS in the state, per PIB reporting on the Delhi Food Department press briefing.

**How to check Delhi ration card status on nfs.delhigovt.nic.in?**

Three routes work. By application number: visit nfs.delhigovt.nic.in, click Track Application, enter your acknowledgment number, view the current status (Received, Under Verification, Verification Complete, Approved, Issued). By Aadhaar number: click Know Your Ration Card, enter your Aadhaar and the captcha. The system returns the ration card number, card type, assigned FPS, and last three PDS transactions if a card exists. By head-of-family mobile: click Login, enter the Aadhaar-seeded mobile number, verify OTP, view the dashboard with e-KYC status and monthly entitlement history.

**How to download my Delhi e-ration card?**

Three routes are available and all are free. State portal: log into nfs.delhigovt.nic.in with your Aadhaar-mobile OTP, navigate to Download e-Ration Card, click Generate PDF, save to device. This is the legally issued copy. Mera Ration 2.0 app: log in with Aadhaar OTP, select My Ration Card, tap Download to save the PDF. DigiLocker: log into digilocker.gov.in with Aadhaar-mobile OTP, search Ration Card in Issued Documents, select Delhi, pull the PDF with the verification QR code. Ignore any third-party site charging a fee.

**What documents are needed for a new Delhi ration card?**

Aadhaar card of every household member, one address proof in the head of family name (voter ID, electricity bill, water bill, gas book, rent agreement, or SDM residence certificate), passport-size family group photograph, and the income declaration form stating annual household income below Rs 2.50 lakh. If applying under AAY, add the applicable criteria proof (widow certificate, disability certificate above 40 percent, senior citizen ID, SC/ST certificate). Bank account number and IFSC of the head of family. Aadhaar-seeded mobile number for OTP-based verification. All uploads accept PDF or JPEG under 2 MB per file.

**What is the PR-S ration card in Delhi?**

Priority-State (PR-S) is Delhi's own state-pool ration card, funded by the GNCTD budget for households that qualify on the income and exclusion criteria but fall outside the central NFSA cap. PR-S cards get the same 5 kg per person per month entitlement as PR cards, and the state pays the differential subsidy from its own budget. Delhi runs roughly 65,000 PR-S cards as of the 15 May 2026 press briefing, and the number is expected to cross 2 lakh by end-FY26 as the fresh issuance drive rolls out through the newly raised Rs 2.50 lakh income ceiling.

**How to add a new family member to my Delhi ration card?**

Log into nfs.delhigovt.nic.in with the head-of-family Aadhaar OTP, navigate to Add Member, enter the new member's Aadhaar number, name, date of birth, and relationship to head of family. Upload the supporting document (birth certificate from the municipal corporation for a newborn, marriage certificate from the sub-registrar for a spouse, Aadhaar plus self-declaration for an elderly parent). Submit. Aadhaar e-KYC of the added member is triggered automatically, so the new member must be available for OTP verification. The addition is verified by the district office within 15 to 30 days, and the service is free.

**What is the Delhi ration card helpline number?**

Two numbers work. 1800-11-0841 is the Department of Food, Supplies and Consumer Affairs toll-free helpline for ration card queries, application status, e-KYC issues, and FPS complaints, available Monday to Saturday 10 AM to 5 PM. 1031 is the Delhi Government citizen grievance helpline covering all state services including PDS, available 24 hours. Both are free from any phone in Delhi. For FPS-specific complaints (short-weighing, dealer refusing entitlement), also use the Consumer Helpline at 1915 or file online at consumerhelpline.gov.in.

**How many new Delhi ration cards is the government issuing in FY26?**

The Delhi government has announced 2 lakh new ration cards for FY26 following the 15 May 2026 relaunch of large-scale issuance after a 13-year freeze, per CM Rekha Gupta's press briefing. Priority is being given to households that (a) applied between 2013 and 2024 and were denied due to the freeze, (b) fall within the newly raised Rs 2.50 lakh income ceiling, and (c) have completed Aadhaar e-KYC. The fresh cards will land primarily in the PR-S state-pool slab since the central NFSA cap for Delhi is largely filled, and PR-S entitlement is identical to PR (5 kg per person per month, free under PMGKAY).

## Primary sources

- Department of Food, Supplies and Consumer Affairs, GNCTD: nfs.delhigovt.nic.in (application, status, e-ration card download, grievance)
- Delhi e-District portal: edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in (Citizen ID registration, income certificate, linked services)
- Delhi Food Security (Amendment) Rules 2026, GNCTD gazette notification (income cap raised Rs 1.20 lakh to Rs 2.50 lakh, effective 13 July 2026)
- PIB press briefing on Delhi ration card relaunch (15 May 2026, CM Rekha Gupta, 2 lakh new cards FY26, 7.72 lakh bogus cancellation)
- National Food Security Portal: nfsa.gov.in (Know Your Ration Card, ONORC portability, national NFSA rules)
- Mera Ration 2.0 app (Google Play Store, Apple App Store) and official FAQ at nfsa.gov.in/doc/FAQ_for_Mera_Ration_2.pdf
- Union Cabinet decision on PMGKAY extension to 31 December 2028 (29 November 2023, outlay Rs 11.80 lakh crore)
- Delhi State Food Commission (statutory grievance body under NFSA Section 16), Vikas Bhawan, Delhi
- Consumer Helpline: 1915, consumerhelpline.gov.in
- Department toll-free 1800-11-0841 and Delhi grievance 1031
